# Dashkit UI - Full Technical Documentation

> Complete API reference, component specifications, CLI commands, and design system tokens for Dashkit.

## Core Architecture & Guidelines

- Source Ownership: Every component is scaffolded directly into your codebase (default `src/dashkit/`).
- Tailwind CSS v4: All styling relies on Tailwind v4 CSS classes, CVA variants, and @variant dark.
- Pure Usage: Rely on built-in component props and variants rather than ad-hoc inline class overrides.
- AI Customization Hierarchy: (1) Edit `dashkit.css` tokens (`--ds-*`, `--radius`) for global theme changes; (2) Edit component `cva(...)` in `src/dashkit/<Component>/` for app-wide component changes; (3) Use `className` and `data-slot` selectors (`[&_[data-slot=label]]:...`) for one-off instance tweaks.
- Block-based Layouts: Use the Card component to partition page sections and views.
- Bun First: Optimized for bun and bunx package management.

## CLI Commands

```bash
# Initialize project
bunx carllosnc/dashkit init

# Add component with unit tests
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add <component> --tests

# Inspect registry in JSON format
bunx carllosnc/dashkit list --json
```

## Components

### Category: Layout & Containers

## Accordion

- Slug: `accordion`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add accordion`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`

# Accordion

A vertically stacked list of headers that reveal associated content areas when clicked.

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Accordion,
  AccordionItem,
  AccordionTrigger,
  AccordionContent
} from '@/dashkit/Accordion'
```

## Installation

Add the accordion to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add accordion
```

## Basic Usage

The accordion supports `single` (default) or `multiple` expansion modes via the `type` prop.


  
    
      Minimalist Performance
      
        No boxes, no shadows. Just clean spacers and thin lines for a modern, high-density dashboard look. We've removed the container styling to let your content breathe.
      
    

    
      Seamless Integration
      
        Designed to fit anywhere—sidebars, settings pages, or complex forms without added visual noise. The spring animations provide a premium feel without being distracting.
      
    

    
      Accessibility First
      
        Fully accessible via keyboard navigation. Users can toggle items using the Enter or Space key, following the standard WAI-ARIA design pattern for accordions.
      
    
  


```tsx
<Accordion type="single" defaultValue="item-1">
  <AccordionItem value="item-1">
    <AccordionTrigger>Minimalist Performance</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      No boxes, no shadows. Just clean spacers and thin lines for a modern, high-density dashboard look.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  {/* ... other items */}
</Accordion>
```

## Multiple

Use the `type="multiple"` prop to allow more than one item to be expanded at the same time.


  
    
      
        
          
          Real-time Updates
        
      
      
        Synchronize state across multiple browser tabs with zero latency using our optimized WebSocket provider.
      
    
    
      
        
          
          Audit Logs Tracking
        
      
      
        Every action is recorded and verifiable. Export logs to CSV or JSON for compliance reporting.
      
    
  


```tsx
<Accordion type="multiple">
  <AccordionItem value="m-1">
    <AccordionTrigger>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <FiZap size={14} />
        <span>Real-time Updates</span>
      </div>
    </AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Synchronize state across multiple browser tabs with zero latency using our optimized WebSocket provider.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  {/* ... other items */}
</Accordion>
```

## Features

- **Height Animations**: Smooth, spring-based expansion using `framer-motion`.
- **Compound Components**: Highly customizable using the sub-component pattern.
- **Multiple Modes**: Toggle between standard accordion behavior or a multi-expand list.
- **Auto-State**: Manages internal open/close state or can be controlled via `value`.
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Fully accessible via enter/space keys and focus management.

## Props

### Accordion



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `type` | `'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'single'` | Expansion logic mode. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` | - | Initial open item(s). |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` | - | Controlled open item(s). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string \| string[]) => void` | - | Event fired on toggle. |



### AccordionItem



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `string` | - | Unique identifier for the item. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Prevents interaction. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom styles for the container. |


## Card

- Slug: `card`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add card`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`
- Dashkit Dependencies: `badge`, `button`

# Card

Dashkit's Card is designed as a **composed wrapper**, providing total layout control through granular sub-components.

## Installation

Add the Card component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add card
```

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardContent,
  CardFooter
} from '@/dashkit/Card';
```

## Basic Usage

The card can be used as a simple container or with its sub-components for more structure.


  
    
      Project Overhaul
      A comprehensive update to the dashboard architecture and visual identity.
    
    
      A standard composed card using the modular component internal structure for full layout control. This design pattern allows for deep nesting and flexible content slots.
    
    
      Dismiss
      View Details
    
  


```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Project Overhaul</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>
      A comprehensive update to the dashboard architecture.
    </CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>
    <p>Card content goes here.</p>
  </CardContent>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button variant="outlined">Dismiss</Button>
    <Button variant="filled">View Details</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

## With Icon & Actions

The `CardHeader` supports a `leftIcon` prop to easily add visual context and an `action` prop for right-aligned elements like badges, buttons, or menus.


  
    }
      action={}
    >
      Security Overview
      Manage your system security settings and firewall rules.
    
    
      Enable advanced threat protection and automated security scanning for all connected infrastructure nodes.
    
  


```tsx
import { FiShield } from 'react-icons/fi';
import { Badge, Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription } from '@dashkit/ui';

<Card>
  <CardHeader 
    leftIcon={<FiShield />}
    action={<Badge content="Enforced" color="success" variant="soft" />}
  >
    <CardTitle>Security Overview</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>
      Manage your system security settings and firewall rules.
    </CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>
    <p>Security details and settings go here.</p>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

## Composable Components

Cards are built using sub-components to provide maximum flexibility for different use cases. While `leftIcon` and `action` handle common patterns, you can still compose the header manually for more complex layouts.


  
    }>
      System Analytics
      Real-time monitoring of global infrastructure and system health.
    
    
      
        
          Uptime
          99.99%
        
        
          Latency
          12ms
        
      
    
    
      View Global Status
    
  


```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader action={<Badge content="Live" color="info" pulse />}>
    <CardTitle>System Analytics</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Real-time infrastructure performance</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>
    {/* Custom grid or data visualization */}
  </CardContent>
  <CardFooter>
     <Button variant="outlined">View Global Status</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

## API Reference

### Card (Root)

The main wrapper container.


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to show a border around the card. |
| `shadowed` | `boolean` | `false` | Apply the modern layered shadow token. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to apply entrance animations. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Root container classes. |


### CardHeader

The top section container.


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `leftIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Optional icon to display on the left of the header content. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | - | Optional content (badge, menu, button) to display on the right of the header. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the header container. |


### CardTitle & CardDescription

Supporting typography components for the header.


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CardTitle` | `h3` | - | Large, bold title with tight tracking. |
| `CardDescription` | `p` | - | Smaller, medium-weight supporting text. |


### CardContent

The main body of the card with standard internal padding and flex growth.


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the content body. |


### CardFooter

The bottom action area with a subtle separator.


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the footer container. |


## Surface

- Slug: `surface`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add surface`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

# Surface

A lightweight, foundational component for creating containers with consistent background variants based on design system states. It provides a clean, borderless surface with no internal padding or margin, serving as a pure visual block.

## Import

```tsx
import { Surface } from '@/dashkit/Surface/Surface'
```

## Installation

Add the surface component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add surface
```

## Basic Usage

The basic surface provides a subtle, borderless background following the theme.



```tsx
<Surface className="h-24">
  Default Surface
</Surface>
```

## State Variants

Surfaces can be styled to represent different states like `info`, `success`, `warning`, and `danger`.



```tsx
<Surface variant="info">Info Content</Surface>
<Surface variant="success">Success Content</Surface>
<Surface variant="warning">Warning Content</Surface>
<Surface variant="danger">Danger Content</Surface>
```

## Custom Styling

Since Surface doesn't provide padding or forced borders, you can easily apply your own layout and border styles.



```tsx
<Surface className="p-8 border border-dashed border-border bg-ds-50/50">
    Customized Block
</Surface>
```

## Props


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'default'` | The visual variant to apply, based on design system states. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The content to be rendered inside the surface. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for custom styling (e.g., padding, width). |


## Divider

- Slug: `divider`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add divider`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

# Divider

A versatile component used to separate sections of content with horizontal or vertical lines.

## Import

```tsx
import { Divider } from '@/dashkit/Divider/Divider'
```

## Installation

Add the divider component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add divider
```

## Basic Usage

The basic horizontal divider represents a solid line.



```tsx
<Divider />
```

## Orientation

Dividers can be horizontal (default) or vertical. For vertical dividers, ensure the parent container has a defined height.



```tsx
<div className="flex items-center h-10 gap-6">
  <span className="text-sm font-medium">Dashboard</span>
  <Divider orientation="vertical" />
  <span className="text-sm font-medium">Settings</span>
</div>
```

## Variants

You can change the visual style of the line using the `variant` prop.



```tsx
<Divider variant="solid" />   {/* Default */}
<Divider variant="dashed" />
<Divider variant="dotted" />
```

## Labels & Content

Horizontal dividers can contain text or other components, positioned along the line.



```tsx
<Divider>Center Label</Divider>
<Divider contentPosition="left">Left Label</Divider>
<Divider contentPosition="right">Right Label</Divider>
```

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | The orientation of the divider. |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'dashed' \| 'dotted'` | `'solid'` | The visual style of the divider line. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Optional content to display in the middle (horizontal only). |
| `contentPosition` | `'left' \| 'center' \| 'right'` | `'center'` | Position of the content relative to the line. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |

- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

        ))}

export const HorizontalExample = () => (
  
    
      
        {Array.from({ length: 10 }).map((_, i) => (
          
            Horizontal Item #{i + 1}
          
        ))}
      
    
  
);

# Scroll Area

A minimalist scroll area component that provides theme-aware, custom scrollbars across all browsers and operating systems.

## Import

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from '@/dashkit/ScrollArea/ScrollArea'
```

## Installation

Add the scroll area to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add scrollarea
```

## Usage

The `ScrollArea` component wraps any content and replaces native scrollbars with a minimalist, theme-aware design while maintaining native scroll performance and accessibility.

### Vertical Scrolling (Default)

The scroll area will automatically handle vertical overflow if the content height exceeds the container height.



```tsx
<div className="h-64 border rounded overflow-hidden">
  <ScrollArea>
    <div className="p-6 space-y-4">
      {/* Long content here */}
    </div>
  </ScrollArea>
</div>
```

### Horizontal Scrolling

Set the `orientation` prop to `horizontal` to enable horizontal scrolling only.



```tsx
<ScrollArea orientation="horizontal" className="h-20">
  <div className="flex gap-4 p-4 w-[1000px]">
    {/* Wide content here */}
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

### Both Orientations

Use `orientation="both"` when you need independent scrolling in both directions.

```tsx
<ScrollArea orientation="both" className="h-64">
  <div className="w-[1000px] h-[1000px] p-8">
    {/* Large two-dimensional content area */}
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

## Features

- **Native Performance**: Uses standard `overflow: auto` for maximum smoothness and accessibility.
- **Theme-Aware**: Automatically switches scrollbar colors based on light/dark mode using project design tokens.
- **Custom Scrollbar Utility**: Leverages the project's `custom-scrollbar` CSS utility for a consistent 4px thin scrollbar.
- **Cross-Browser**: Standardizes appearance across modern browsers.
- **Low Dependency**: Zero external libraries; depends only on core project utilities.

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | The scroll direction allowed in the area. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the outer container. |
| `viewportClassName` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the scrollable viewport. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The content to be scrolled. |


### Category: Navigation

## Navbar

- Slug: `navbar`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add navbar`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`, `class-variance-authority`

# Navbar

A premium, responsive navigation header with support for branding, navigation, and action buttons using a flexible composition pattern.

## Import

```tsx
import { Navbar, NavbarBrand, NavbarLinks, NavbarActions } from '@/dashkit/Navbar/Navbar'
```

## Installation

Add the navbar to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add navbar
```

## Basic Usage

The `Navbar` uses a composition pattern, allowing you to easily arrange branding, links, and actions.



```tsx
<Navbar>
  <NavbarBrand>
    <span className="font-bold">Dashkit</span>
  </NavbarBrand>

  <NavbarLinks>
    <a href="/docs">Docs</a>
    <a href="/examples">Examples</a>
  </NavbarLinks>

  <NavbarActions>
    <Button size="sm">Explore</Button>
  </NavbarActions>
</Navbar>
```

## With Icons & Actions

You can combine text links with icon buttons and utilities in the actions area.



```tsx
import { FiGithub, FiBell } from 'react-icons/fi';

<Navbar>
  <NavbarBrand>Acme Corp</NavbarBrand>
  
  <NavbarActions>
     <IconButton icon={<FiBell size={18} />} size="sm" variant="ghost" />
     <Divider orientation="vertical" className="h-6" />
     <IconButton icon={<FiGithub size={18} />} size="sm" variant="ghost" />
  </NavbarActions>
</Navbar>
```

## Features

- **Responsive Design**: Links are automatically hidden on smaller screens while branding and actions remain.
- **Backdrop Blur**: Optional glassmorphism effect using the `blur` prop.
- **Sticky Behavior**: Automatically sticks to the top of its parent container or viewport.
- **Composition Based**: Use semantic sub-components for full layout control.

## Components Breakdown

The Navbar library includes several specialized sections:


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Navbar` | - | - | The root container that handles height, backdrop blur, and sticky behavior. |
| `NavbarBrand` | - | - | Used for logos, brand names, and mobile menu triggers. |
| `NavbarLinks` | - | - | A responsive container for navigation items (hidden on mobile). |
| `NavbarActions` | - | - | Container for utility icons, themes, and primary action buttons. |


## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the navbar sticks to the top of the viewport. |
| `blur` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to apply glassmorphism backdrop blur. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the header container. |


## NavigationMenu

- Slug: `navigation-menu`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add navigation-menu`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`

# Navigation Menu

A premium navigation menu component inspired by modern, high-end dashboards. It features a shared viewport that smoothly moves and resizes to accommodate different content sections.

## Import

```tsx
import {
  NavigationMenu,
  NavigationMenuList,
  NavigationMenuItem,
  NavigationMenuTrigger,
  NavigationMenuContent,
  NavigationMenuLink,
  NavigationMenuViewport
} from '@/dashkit/NavigationMenu/NavigationMenu'
```

## Installation

Add the navigation menu to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add navigation-menu
```

## Basic Usage

The Navigation Menu uses a value-based system to track the active item. Ensure the `value` on `NavigationMenuTrigger` matches the `value` on `NavigationMenuContent`.

```tsx
<NavigationMenu>
  <NavigationMenuList>
    <NavigationMenuItem>
      <NavigationMenuTrigger value="solutions">Solutions</NavigationMenuTrigger>
      <NavigationMenuContent value="solutions">
        <div className="w-[300px] p-4 flex flex-col gap-2">
           <NavigationMenuLink href="/solutions/saas">SaaS</NavigationMenuLink>
           <NavigationMenuLink href="/solutions/enterprise">Enterprise</NavigationMenuLink>
        </div>
      </NavigationMenuContent>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
    {/* ... other items */}
  </NavigationMenuList>

  <NavigationMenuViewport />
</NavigationMenu>
```

## Props

### NavigationMenu

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `delay` | `number` | `200` | Delay in milliseconds before closing the menu after the mouse leaves. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the root container. |

### NavigationMenuTrigger

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `string` | - | A unique value to associate the trigger with its corresponding content. |

### NavigationMenuContent

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `string` | - | The unique value matching the NavigationMenuTrigger. |

# Sidebar

A versatile and premium navigation sidebar component that supports complex layouts, branding, status indicators, and responsive mobile drawer adaptation out of the box.

## Import

```tsx
import { 
  Sidebar,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarHeader, 
  SidebarHeaderOpen, 
  SidebarHeaderClose, 
  SidebarFooter, 
  SidebarFooterOpen, 
  SidebarFooterClose, 
  SidebarSection, 
  SidebarItem,
  SidebarSubList,
  SidebarSubItem,
  useSidebar
} from '@/dashkit/Sidebar/Sidebar'
```

## Installation

Add the sidebar into your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add sidebar
```

## Basic Usage

The `Sidebar` uses a semantic composition of headers, content scroll area, sections, and footers to create a cohesive navigation experience.





```tsx
import { Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarSection, SidebarItem } from '@/dashkit';
import { FiLayout, FiActivity, FiSettings } from 'react-icons/fi';

export default function App() {
  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState('dashboard');

  return (
    <Sidebar className="w-64 border-r">
      <SidebarHeader>
        <Logo />
        <span>Dashkit</span>
      </SidebarHeader>

      <SidebarContent>
        <SidebarSection title="General">
          <SidebarItem
            icon={<FiLayout />}
            active={activeTab === 'dashboard'}
            onClick={() => setActiveTab('dashboard')}
          >
            Overview
          </SidebarItem>
        </SidebarSection>
      </SidebarContent>
    </Sidebar>
  );
}
```

## Responsive Mobile Drawer

By default (`responsive={true}`), the `Sidebar` automatically adapts between desktop and mobile devices:
- **Desktop (≥ 768px)**: Sits in the layout flow and smoothly expands or collapses between `width` (272px) and `collapsedWidth` (72px).
- **Mobile (< 768px)**: Disappears from the layout flow so the main content takes full width, and opens as an accessible sliding **Drawer with Backdrop Blur** via ``.
- Supports focus management, `Escape` key to close, swipe gestures, and dynamic viewport heights (`100dvh`).

```tsx
import { SidebarProvider, Sidebar, SidebarTrigger, SidebarContent, SidebarHeader, SidebarSection, SidebarItem } from '@/dashkit';
import { Navbar, NavbarBrand } from '@/dashkit';

export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider>
      <div className="flex h-screen w-full">
        {/* On desktop: in-flow collapsible sidebar. On mobile: portal Drawer */}
        <Sidebar>
          <SidebarHeader>My App</SidebarHeader>
          <SidebarContent>
            <SidebarSection title="Menu">
              <SidebarItem icon={<FiLayout />}>Dashboard</SidebarItem>
            </SidebarSection>
          </SidebarContent>
        </Sidebar>

        <div className="flex-1 flex flex-col min-w-0">
          <Navbar>
            <NavbarBrand>
              {/* Toggles sidebar on desktop or opens Drawer on mobile */}
              <SidebarTrigger />
              <span>Dashboard</span>
            </NavbarBrand>
          </Navbar>

          <main className="flex-1 p-6">
            {children}
          </main>
        </div>
      </div>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}
```

## Collapsible Sidebar

Enable the `collapsible` prop to show a floating toggle button on the desktop sidebar edge. You can use the `isOpen` state to conditionally render content using native utility components.

```tsx
<Sidebar collapsible defaultOpen={true}>
  <SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarHeaderOpen>Full Branding</SidebarHeaderOpen>
    <SidebarHeaderClose>Logo</SidebarHeaderClose>
  </SidebarHeader>
  {/* ... items ... */}
</Sidebar>
```

## Collapsible Sections

Sections can be individually collapsed to conserve vertical space or group related functionality. Use the `collapsible` prop on `SidebarSection` to enable this behavior. You can also control the initial expansion state with the `defaultOpen` prop.



```tsx
<SidebarSection title="Account" collapsible>
  <SidebarItem icon={<FiUser />}>Profile</SidebarItem>
  <SidebarItem icon={<FiShield />}>Security</SidebarItem>
</SidebarSection>

<SidebarSection title="Settings" collapsible defaultOpen={false}>
  <SidebarItem icon={<FiSettings />}>Advanced</SidebarItem>
</SidebarSection>
```

## Components Breakdown

The Sidebar library is composed of several specialized layers designed for specific layout roles:


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SidebarProvider` | - | - | Context provider for coordinating state between Sidebar and external triggers. |
| `Sidebar` | - | - | The main container that handles desktop collapse and mobile drawer portal. |
| `SidebarTrigger` | - | - | Accessible button to toggle the sidebar collapse (desktop) or mobile drawer. |
| `SidebarContent` | - | - | Scrollable flex-1 body for navigation sections and items. |
| `SidebarHeader` | - | - | Designed for branding, logos, organization switchers, and mobile dismiss. |
| `SidebarHeaderOpen/Close` | - | - | Conditional wrappers that show content based on sidebar expansion. |
| `SidebarFooter` | - | - | Bottom section for user profiles, help links, or versioning. |
| `SidebarFooterOpen/Close` | - | - | Conditional wrappers for specialized footer layouts. |
| `SidebarSection` | - | - | Groups related items with an optional title. |
| `SidebarItem` | - | - | Individual navigation links, optionally collapsible with sub-items. |
| `SidebarSubList` | - | - | Vertical tree-guide container for indented sub-items. |
| `SidebarSubItem` | - | - | Sub-navigation link styled for nested tree hierarchies. |


## API Reference

### Sidebar


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The content of the sidebar. |
| `responsive` | `boolean` | `true` | Automatically switches to an overlay Drawer with Backdrop on mobile. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows a floating toggle button on the desktop edge. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | Initial state for uncontrolled desktop sidebar. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state for desktop sidebar. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Event handler for desktop state changes. |
| `defaultOpenMobile` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state for mobile drawer. |
| `openMobile` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state for mobile drawer. |
| `onOpenMobileChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Event handler for mobile drawer state changes. |
| `mobileBreakpoint` | `number` | `768` | Screen width breakpoint in px below which mobile drawer activates. |
| `width` | `number` | `272` | Expanded width of the desktop sidebar in pixels. |
| `collapsedWidth` | `number` | `72` | Collapsed width of the desktop sidebar in pixels. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the container. |

", "description": "Custom icon for the trigger button." },
    { "prop": "className", "type": "string", "defaultValue": "—", "description": "Custom class names for the button." }
  ]}
/>

### SidebarSection

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

## Breadcrumb

- Slug: `breadcrumb`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add breadcrumb`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`, `class-variance-authority`

# Breadcrumb

A secondary navigation component that helps users understand their current location in the application hierarchy.

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
  BreadcrumbEllipsis
} from '@/dashkit/Breadcrumb'
```

## Installation

Add the breadcrumb to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add breadcrumb
```

## Basic Usage

The `Breadcrumb` component uses a composition pattern. `BreadcrumbItem` can automatically render as a link if an `href` is provided.



```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem href="/docs">Components</BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem active>Breadcrumb</BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## With Icons

You can add icons to your breadcrumb items by passing them as children alongside the text.



```tsx
import { FiHome, FiSettings, FiUser } from 'react-icons/fi';

<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem href="/">
      <FiHome size={14} /> Home
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem href="/settings">
      <FiSettings size={14} /> Settings
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem active>
      <FiUser size={14} /> Profile
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Custom Separator

Override the default separator with any React node.



```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator>
    <BreadcrumbItem active>Components</BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Collapsed (Ellipsis)

Use `BreadcrumbEllipsis` to show a collapsed state for long paths.



```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem active>Active Page</BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Simplified Usage (Legacy)

You can still use the `items` prop for simpler cases.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={[
    { label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { label: 'Components', href: '/docs' },
    { label: 'Breadcrumb' },
  ]}
/>
```

## API

### Breadcrumb Props


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The composition of BreadcrumbList and items. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |


### BreadcrumbList Props


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The items and separators. |


### BreadcrumbItem Props


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `href` | `string` | - | Optional URL for the breadcrumb link. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the item is the current page. |


## Tabs

- Slug: `tabs`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add tabs`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

# Tabs

A performant and premium tabs component with a smooth, fluid indicator animation powered by Framer Motion.

## Import

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@/dashkit/Tabs/Tabs'
```

## Installation

Add the tabs to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add tabs
```

## Basic Usage

The component is highly accessible and supports a fluid layout for its triggers.


  
    
      Account
      Password
    
    
      Account Settings
      Update your account email and personal information.
    
    
      Password
      Change your password and manage your security settings.
    
  


```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="account">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="account">Account</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="password">Password</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="account">
    Manage your account data.
  </TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="password">
    Change your password.
  </TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

## Icons & Advanced Previews

You can easily integrate icons and complex child layouts within your tabs.


  
    
      
        
        Profile
      
      
        
        Activity
      
      
        
        Settings
      
    

    
      User Profile
      
        Update your personal details and public information. All changes are saved automatically.
      
    
    
      Recent Activity
      
        
          
          Successfully deployed project dashkit
        
        
          
          Updated registry.json
        
      
    
    
      Preferences
      
        Manage your notification types, connected accounts, and general dashboard settings.
      
    
  


```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="profile">
  <TabsList className="w-full">
    <TabsTrigger value="profile">
      <FiUser className="mr-2 size-4" />
      Profile
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="activity">
      <FiActivity className="mr-2 size-4" />
      Activity
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="settings">
      <FiSettings className="mr-2 size-4" />
      Settings
    </TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
</Tabs>
```

## Animated Indicators

The indicator uses Framer Motion's `layoutId` to achieve a "sliding" effect when transitioning between tabs. This happens automatically when triggers are within the same `Tabs` root.

## Props

### Tabs



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | The value of the tab that should be active on mount. |
| `value` | `string` | - | The controlled value of the active tab. |
| `onValueChange` | `(val: string) => void` | - | Callback fired when the active tab changes. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Content of the tabs container. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |



### TabsTrigger



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `string` | - | A unique value that identifies this tab. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Content for the tab trigger button. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the trigger button. |


## Stepper

- Slug: `stepper`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add stepper`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`

# Stepper

A progress visualization component for multi-step processes or sequence indicators.

## Import

```tsx
import { Stepper, Step } from '@/dashkit/Stepper'
```

## Installation

Add the stepper to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add stepper
```

## Quick Start
Displays a multi-step sequence with active, completed, and inactive states. Uses `framer-motion` for animated connecting lines.


  
    {React.createElement(() => {
      const [step, setStep] = useState(1);
      return (
        
           
              
              
              
           
           
           
               setStep(prev => prev - 1)}>Back
               setStep(prev => prev + 1)}>Next Step
           
        
      );
    })}
  


```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Stepper, Step } from '@/dashkit/Stepper';
import { Button } from '@/dashkit/Button/Button';

export function StepperExample() {
  const [step, setStep] = useState(1);

  return (
    <div className="w-full space-y-8">
       <Stepper activeStep={step} onChange={setStep}>
          <Step title="Sign Up" description="Create your account" />
          <Step title="Payment" description="Add funding source" />
          <Step title="Complete" description="Explore dashboard" />
       </Stepper>
       
       <div className="flex gap-2 justify-end">
          <Button variant="outlined" disabled={step === 0} onClick={() => setStep(prev => prev - 1)}>Back</Button>
          <Button disabled={step === 2} onClick={() => setStep(prev => prev + 1)}>Next Step</Button>
       </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Vertical Orientation
Set `orientation="vertical"` to stack the steps vertically, which is highly suited for sidebars or logs.


  
    
      
      
      
      
    
  


```tsx
import { Stepper, Step } from '@/dashkit/Stepper';

<Stepper activeStep={2} orientation="vertical">
  <Step title="Order Placed" description="Order #32049 has been confirmed." />
  <Step title="Processing" description="Your package is being prepared." />
  <Step title="In Transit" description="Package left local facility." />
  <Step title="Delivered" description="Package arrived." />
</Stepper>
```

## Custom Icons
By default, steps are auto-numbered. You can supply an `icon` prop to customize the visual indicator for each step.


  
    
      } />
      } />
      } />
    
  


```tsx
import { Stepper, Step } from '@/dashkit/Stepper';
import { FiUser, FiCreditCard, FiCheckCircle } from 'react-icons/fi';

<Stepper activeStep={1}>
  <Step title="Profile" icon={<FiUser size={14} />} />
  <Step title="Billing" icon={<FiCreditCard size={14} />} />
  <Step title="Success" icon={<FiCheckCircle size={14} />} />
</Stepper>
```

## Color Palettes

Control the stepper's accent theme using the `color` prop. Use `"primary"` (default) for brand accenting or `"base"` for clean, monochrome neutral styling.


  
    Base Monochrome Theme (`color="base"`)
    
      
      
      
    
  


```tsx
<Stepper activeStep={1} color="base">
  <Step title="Configuration" description="Setup parameters" />
  <Step title="Verification" description="Review cluster state" />
  <Step title="Deployment" description="Rollout to edge" />
</Stepper>
```

## Clickable Navigation
If you provide an `onChange` handler, steps become fully interactive and users can jump between them by clicking.
```tsx
const [activeStep, setActiveStep] = useState(0);

// Users can now click the steps to jump freely!
<Stepper activeStep={activeStep} onChange={setActiveStep}>
  <Step title="First" />
  <Step title="Second" />
</Stepper>
```

## Props

### Stepper


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `activeStep` | `number` | - | Index of the currently active step (0-indexed). |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Layout orientation of the stepper. |
| `onChange` | `(step: number) => void` | - | Optional callback fired when a step is clicked. Adding this makes steps interactive. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes merged via clsx. |


### Step


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | - | Main label of the step. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Secondary description rendered below the title. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Custom icon element (e.g., Avatar or SVG). Replaces the default numbered circle. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the step wrapper. |


## Pagination

- Slug: `pagination`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add pagination`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`, `framer-motion`

# Pagination

A functional and responsive component for navigating between large sets of data or views.

## Quick Start
Provide the `currentPage`, `totalPages`, and an `onChange` callback to sync state perfectly.


  {React.createElement(() => {
    const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
    return (
      
    );
  })}


```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pagination } from '@/dashkit/Pagination';

export function PaginationExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);

  return (
    <Pagination 
      currentPage={page} 
      totalPages={10} 
      onChange={setPage} 
    />
  );
}
```

## Short List
When `totalPages` is small (e.g., 5 pages), the component automatically hides the ellipsis logic and simply renders a cohesive string of pages.


  {React.createElement(() => {
    const [page, setPage] = useState(2);
    return (
      
    );
  })}


```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pagination } from '@/dashkit/Pagination';

export function PaginationShortExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(2);

  return (
    <Pagination 
      currentPage={page} 
      totalPages={5} 
      onChange={setPage} 
    />
  );
}
```

## Large Data Ranges
The `Pagination` component automatically calculates ellipsis (`...`) truncations for large ranges to prevent overflowing.


  {React.createElement(() => {
    const [page, setPage] = useState(50);
    return (
      
    );
  })}


```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pagination } from '@/dashkit/Pagination';

export function PaginationLargeDataExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(50);

  return (
    <Pagination 
      currentPage={page} 
      totalPages={100} 
      onChange={setPage} 
    />
  );
}
```

## Minimal Mode
By configuring `siblingCount={0}`, you can minimize the footprint of the pagination. The component defaults to `siblingCount={1}`.


  {React.createElement(() => {
    const [page, setPage] = useState(25);
    return (
      
    );
  })}


```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pagination } from '@/dashkit/Pagination';

export function PaginationMinimalExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(25);

  return (
    <Pagination 
      currentPage={page} 
      totalPages={50} 
      siblingCount={0}
      onChange={setPage} 
    />
  );
}
```

## Props


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `currentPage` | `number` | - | The currently active page (1-indexed). |
| `totalPages` | `number` | - | Total number of pages. |
| `onChange` | `(page: number) => void` | - | Callback fired when a page is clicked or next/prev is activated. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | Number of sibling pages to show on each side of the active page. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the navigation wrapper. |

- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add dock`

# Dock

A fluid, magnified navigation bar inspired by macOS, using Framer Motion for high-fidelity interactive physics.

## Import

```tsx
import { Dock, DockItem } from '@/dashkit/Dock/Dock';
```

## Installation

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add dock
```

## Basic Usage

The dock is composed of a `Dock` container and multiple `DockItem` components.



```tsx
<Dock>
  <DockItem icon={<FiHome />} label="Home" />
  <DockItem icon={<FiCommand />} label="Terminal" />
  <DockItem icon={<FiGrid />} label="Dashboard" />
  <DockItem icon={<FiGithub />} label="GitHub" href="https://github.com" />
</Dock>
```

## Theme Inversion

The Dock component implements an inverted contrast theme by default:
- **Light mode**: Uses dark backgrounds and light icons/text.
- **Dark mode**: Uses white backgrounds and dark icons/text.

This makes the dock stand out visually from the rest of the UI, behaving more like a floating control utility.

## Customization

You can adjust the `magnification` (how much it grows) and the `distance` (how far the magnet reach is).

```tsx
<Dock magnification={80} distance={200}>
  <DockItem icon={<FiHome />} />
</Dock>
```

## Features

- **Fluid Magnification**: Uses `framer-motion`'s `useSpring` and `useTransform` for physics-based scaling.
- **Smart Positioning**: Items adjust their width relative to the cursor position on the `X` axis.
- **Tooltips Included**: Built-in hover labels for quick identification of icon-only items.
- **Theme Logic**: Specialized colors that provide high contrast in both themes.
- **Composed API**: Clean JSX structure for easy item management.

## Component API

### Dock


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `position` | `'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `'bottom'` | The visual alignment of the dock. Vertical positions switch tracking to the Y axis. |
| `magnification` | `number` | `60` | The maximum width of an item when the mouse is directly over it. |
| `distance` | `number` | `140` | The distance from the mouse where the magnification effect starts. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the dock container. |


### DockItem


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon component to display inside the dock item. |
| `label` | `string` | - | A text label that appears on hover. |
| `href` | `string` | - | If provided, the item will render as an anchor link. |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | - | Callback function when the item is clicked. |


### Category: Forms & Inputs

## Button

- Slug: `button`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add button`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`, `react-icons`
- Dashkit Dependencies: `spinner`

# Button

A highly customizable button component supporting multiple variants, icons, and loading states.

## Import

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/dashkit/Button/Button'
```

## Installation

Add the button to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add button
```

## Variants

Use the `variant` prop to switch between visual styles.



```tsx
<Button variant="filled">Filled</Button>
<Button variant="outlined">Outlined</Button>
<Button variant="soft">Soft</Button>
```

## With Icons

Use `leftIcon` and `rightIcon` to add icons before or after the label.



```tsx
import { FiDownload, FiArrowRight } from 'react-icons/fi'

<Button variant="filled" leftIcon={<FiDownload />}>
  Download Data
</Button>

<Button variant="outlined" rightIcon={<FiArrowRight />}>
  Next Step
</Button>
```

## Loading State

Set the `loading` prop to show a spinner and disable the button. When loading, the left icon is replaced by the spinner and the right icon is hidden.



```tsx
<Button variant="filled" loading>
  Saving Changes
</Button>
```

## Disabled

Use the native `disabled` prop. The button becomes non-interactive with reduced opacity.



```tsx
<Button variant="filled" disabled>Filled Disabled</Button>
<Button variant="outlined" disabled>Outlined Disabled</Button>
```

## Icon Only

If you omit the `children` (label) and provide only an icon, the button will automatically switch to a circular/square layout with balanced padding. **Note:** Always provide an `aria-label` for accessibility when using icon-only buttons.



```tsx
<Button variant="filled" leftIcon={<FiDownload />} aria-label="Download" />
<Button variant="outlined" leftIcon={<FiArrowRight />} aria-label="Next" />
```

## Rounded Corner Styles

Buttons use fully rounded pill shapes by default. Pass `rounded={false}` for crisp medium-rounded corners.



```tsx
<Button variant="filled">Pill (Default)</Button>
<Button variant="filled" rounded={false}>Medium Rounded</Button>
```

## Custom Styling

You can easily override or extend the default styles using the `className` prop. The component uses `tailwind-merge` internally, so your custom classes will automatically take precedence over the defaults without needing the `!` (important) modifier.



```tsx
// Custom classes automatically override defaults thanks to tailwind-merge
<Button className="rounded-xl bg-indigo-600 hover:bg-indigo-700">
  Custom Radius & Color
</Button>

<Button variant="outlined" className="border-red-500 text-red-500 hover:bg-red-50">
  Destructive Action
</Button>
```

## Props

The component extends all native `ButtonHTMLAttributes` props (e.g. `onClick`, `type`, `disabled`, `className`), plus the following:



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `variant` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'soft'` | `'filled'` | Visual style of the button. |
| `leftIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon element rendered before the label. Replaced by spinner when loading. |
| `rightIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon element rendered after the label. Hidden when loading. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a spinner, disables the button, and hides icons. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the button with reduced opacity. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes merged via clsx. |
| `ref` | `Ref` | - | Forwarded ref to the underlying  element. |


## IconButton

- Slug: `iconbutton`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add iconbutton`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`, `react-icons`

# Icon Button

A premium, specialized button for icon-only actions with customizable variant and rounding options.

## Import

```tsx
import { IconButton } from '@/dashkit/IconButton/IconButton'
```

## Installation

Add the icon button component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add icon-button
```

## Basic Usage

Icon buttons are compact triggers that display only an icon. They are perfect for toolbars and navigation.



```tsx
import { FiBell, FiSettings, FiShare2 } from 'react-icons/fi';

<IconButton icon={<FiBell />} variant="filled" />
<IconButton icon={<FiEdit />} variant="outlined" />
<IconButton icon={<FiSettings />} variant="soft" />
<IconButton icon={<FiShare2 />} variant="ghost" />
```

## Variants

Choose between four distinct visual styles: `filled`, `outlined`, `soft`, and `ghost`.



```tsx
<IconButton icon={<FiEdit />} variant="filled" />
<IconButton icon={<FiEdit />} variant="outlined" />
<IconButton icon={<FiEdit />} variant="soft" />
<IconButton icon={<FiEdit />} variant="ghost" />
```

## Shapes

The `rounded` prop allows you to switch between a rounded-square (default) and a full circular shape.



```tsx
<IconButton icon={<FiTrash />} rounded={false} />
<IconButton icon={<FiTrash />} rounded={true} />
```

## States

Icon buttons can be disabled to prevent user interaction while remaining visually consistent.



```tsx
<IconButton icon={<FiSettings />} disabled />
<IconButton icon={<FiTrash />} variant="filled" disabled />
```

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon component to render inside the button. |
| `variant` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'soft' \| 'ghost'` | `'soft'` | Visual style variant of the button. |
| `rounded` | `boolean` | `false` | If true, applies rounded-full (circular), otherwise rounded-md. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button is interactive. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |
| `onClick` | `function` | - | Standard click event handler. |


## ButtonGroup

- Slug: `buttongroup`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add buttongroup`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

# Button Group

The **ButtonGroup** component is used to cluster multiple buttons together in a single, cohesive unit. This is often used for toolbar actions, toggle switches, or navigation. It features a modern, border-aware outlined design with dedicated selection states.

## Examples

### Segmented Control

One of the most common uses for a button group is to switch between different views or filters. Use `flex-1` on the items to create equal-width segments.



```tsx
<ButtonGroup className="w-full">
  <ButtonGroupItem className="flex-1" selected>Activity</ButtonGroupItem>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="flex-1">Analytics</ButtonGroupItem>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="flex-1">History</ButtonGroupItem>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### View Switcher

Combine icons and text for a more descriptive interface. The selection state uses a subtle primary background to indicate the active choice.



```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="gap-2" selected>
    <FiGrid size={16} /> Grid
  </ButtonGroupItem>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="gap-2">
    <FiList size={16} /> List
  </ButtonGroupItem>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="gap-2">
    <FiLayout size={16} /> Compact
  </ButtonGroupItem>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Formatting Toolbar

Button groups are essential for toolbars. The `-space-x-px` logic ensures borders never double up, maintaining a crisp appearance.



### Vertical Stack

Vertical groups are useful for sidebars or property menus.



```tsx
<ButtonGroup vertical>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="justify-start">Top Action</ButtonGroupItem>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="justify-start" selected>Active State</ButtonGroupItem>
  <ButtonGroupItem className="justify-start">Bottom Action</ButtonGroupItem>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## Props

### ButtonGroup


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The buttons to be grouped together. |
| `vertical` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the buttons should be stacked vertically. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |


### ButtonGroupItem


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Content of the button. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button is in a selected state. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the button. |


## Input

- Slug: `input`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add input`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`, `react-icons`

export const PatternsExample = () => {
  const formatCPF = (val) => val
    .replace(/^(\d{3})(\d)/, '$1.$2')
    .replace(/^(\d{3})\.(\d{3})(\d)/, '$1.$2.$3')
    .replace(/\.(\d{3})(\d)/, '.$1-$2')
    .slice(0, 14);

  const formatPhone = (val) => {
    if (val.length <= 10) {
      return val.replace(/^(\d{2})(\d)/, '($1) $2').replace(/(\d{4})(\d)/, '$1-$2').slice(0, 14);
    }
    return val.replace(/^(\d{2})(\d)/, '($1) $2').replace(/(\d{5})(\d)/, '$1-$2').slice(0, 15);
  };

  return (
    
      
      
    
  );
};

# Input

A primitive input component with support for labels, icons, error states, and helper text.

## Import

```tsx
import { Input } from '@/dashkit/Input/Input'
```

## Installation

Add the input component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add input
```

## Basic Usage

The basic usage of the input with a label and placeholder.



```tsx
<Input 
  label="Email Address" 
  placeholder="Enter your email" 
/>
```

## With Icons

Use `leftIcon` and `rightIcon` to add icons to the input. The icons automatically transition their color when the input is focused.



```tsx
import { FiSearch, FiLock } from 'react-icons/fi'

<Input 
  label="Search" 
  placeholder="Search..." 
  leftIcon={<FiSearch />} 
/>

<Input 
  label="Password" 
  type="password" 
  rightIcon={<FiLock />} 
/>
```

## States

The input supports error and disabled states.



```tsx
<Input 
  label="Username" 
  error="Username is already taken" 
  defaultValue="carllosnc" 
/>

<Input 
  label="API Key" 
  disabled 
  value="sk_test_51Mz..." 
  helperText="You cannot edit this key" 
/>
```

## Custom Styling

You can override or extend the styles of the input via `className`.



```tsx
<Input 
  className="rounded-full border-indigo-200 focus:border-indigo-500 focus:ring-indigo-100" 
  placeholder="Custom style"
/>
```

## Masking & Formatting

The input component provides built-in support for masking (to filter characters) and formatting (to transform the displayed string).

### Digit Only Mask



```tsx
<Input 
  label="Numeric Only" 
  mask={/[^\d]/g} 
  placeholder="123..." 
/>
```

### Complex Patterns

Using `mask` and `formatter` together enables masking for specific formats like Brasil CPF and phone numbers.



```tsx
const formatCPF = (val) => {
  return val
    .replace(/^(\d{3})(\d)/, '$1.$2')
    .replace(/^(\d{3})\.(\d{3})(\d)/, '$1.$2.$3')
    .replace(/\.(\d{3})(\d)/, '.$1-$2')
    .slice(0, 14);
};

<Input 
  label="CPF (Brasil)" 
  mask={/[^\d]/g}
  formatter={formatCPF}
  placeholder="000.000.000-00" 
/>
```

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `label` | `string` | - | Input label rendered above the field. |
| `leftIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon element rendered at the start of the field. |
| `rightIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon element rendered at the end of the field. |
| `mask` | `RegExp` | - | Regex used to filter input values (matches are removed). |
| `formatter` | `(val) => string` | - | Function to format the value after masking. |
| `error` | `string` | - | Error message displayed below the field. |
| `helperText` | `string` | - | Helper message displayed below the field. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the input element. |
| `ref` | `Ref` | - | Forwarded ref to the underlying  element. |

         setChecked(true)}

# Checkbox

A custom-styled checkbox component for binary choices, with support for labels and descriptions.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@/dashkit/Checkbox/Checkbox'
```

## Installation

Add the checkbox component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add checkbox
```

## Basic Usage

The basic checkbox with a label.



```tsx
<Checkbox label="Remember me" />
```

## With Description

You can add a description below the label to provide more context.



```tsx
<Checkbox 
  label="Accept terms and conditions" 
  description="You agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy." 
/>
```

## States

The checkbox supports various states like checked, disabled, and focus.



```tsx
<Checkbox label="Default Checked" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Disabled Unchecked" disabled />
<Checkbox label="Disabled Checked" disabled defaultChecked />
```

## Custom Styling

You can override or extend styles via `className`.



```tsx
<Checkbox 
  label="Indigo Variant" 
  className="peer-checked:bg-indigo-600 peer-checked:border-indigo-600" 
  defaultChecked 
/>
```

## Controlled

You can use the `checked` and `onChange` props to control the checkbox state with React.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'

export function ControlledCheckbox() {
  const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false)

  return (
    <Checkbox 
      label="Controlled Checkbox" 
      description={`Currently: ${checked ? 'Checked' : 'Unchecked'}`}
      checked={checked}
      onChange={(e) => setChecked(e.target.checked)}
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

The component extends all native `InputHTMLAttributes` props (excluding `type`), plus the following:



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `label` | `string` | - | Label rendered to the right of the checkbox. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Additional context rendered below the label. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the checkbox container. |
| `ref` | `Ref` | - | Forwarded ref to the underlying  element. |

  ];

         setSelected(opt.id)}
        />
      ))}
    
  );
}

# Radio


## Installation

Add the radio button to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add radio
```

## Basic Usage

The basic radio button with a label. Usually part of a group sharing the same `name`.



```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <Radio label="Option 1" name="radio-group" value="1" defaultChecked />
  <Radio label="Option 2" name="radio-group" value="2" />
</div>
```

## With Description

You can add descriptions for more complex choices.



```tsx
<Radio 
  label="Priority Shipping" 
  description="Next day delivery by morning" 
  name="shipping" 
  value="priority" 
/>
```

## States

Supports checked, disabled, and focus states.



```tsx
<Radio label="Default Checked" defaultChecked />
<Radio label="Disabled Unchecked" disabled />
<Radio label="Disabled Checked" disabled defaultChecked />
```

## Controlled

Works seamlessly with React's state management.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'

export function LanguageSelection() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('react')

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <Radio 
        label="React" 
        checked={value === 'react'} 
        onChange={() => setValue('react')} 
      />
      <Radio 
        label="Vue" 
        checked={value === 'vue'} 
        onChange={() => setValue('vue')} 
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

| `ref` | `Ref` | - | Forwarded ref to the underlying radio input. |

# Select

A high-performance dropdown component for single choices, featuring portalled rendering to prevent layout overflow and full keyboard accessibility.

## Import

```tsx
import { Select } from '@/dashkit/Select/Select'
```

## Installation

Add the select component using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add select
```

## Examples

### Shipping Configuration

A standard implementation with labels, descriptions, and controlled state.



```tsx
export function ShippingForm() {
  const [method, setMethod] = useState('');
  
  return (
    <Select 
      label="Shipping Method"
      placeholder="Select method..."
      options={[
        { value: 'ground', label: 'Ground (3-5 days)' },
        { value: 'air', label: 'Air (Next day)' }
      ]}
      value={method}
      onChange={setMethod}
    />
  );
}
```

## Features

- **Portalled Rendering**: Renders the dropdown list using `createPortal` to the `document.body`, ensuring it stays on top of all other elements regardless of container overflow.
- **Dynamic Positioning**: Automatically calculates the trigger's position to align the popup accurately.
- **Interaction Guards**: Automatically closes the menu when the user scrolls or clicks outside to preserve UI intent.
- **Keyboard Friendly**: Fully supports `Enter`, `Space`, and `Escape` keys for navigation without a pointer.
- **Empty State Support**: Built-in messaging when no options are provided.

## Properties


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `options` | `SelectOption[]` | - | List of available choices (value and label). |
| `value` | `string` | - | The current selected value. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Callback triggered when a new option is chosen. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `'Select an option'` | Text shown when no option is selected. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Bold header text above the component. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Subtle context text below the component. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Prevents all interaction with the dropdown. |

# Combobox

A combobox is a flexible select component that allows users to filter a large list of options via a search input.

## Import

```tsx
import { Combobox } from '@/dashkit/Combobox/Combobox'
```

## Installation

Add the combobox component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add combobox
```

## Basic Search

The component behaves like a standard select, but with a built-in search input to handle long lists of data.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';

const frameworks = [
  { value: 'nextjs', label: 'Next.js' },
  { value: 'vite', label: 'Vite' },
  { value: 'astro', label: 'Astro' },
];

export const BasicExample = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('nextjs');
  return (
    <Combobox
      label="Frontend Framework"
      options={frameworks}
      value={value}
      onChange={setValue}
    />
  );
};
```

## Multi-Selection

Use the `multiple` prop to allow users to select more than one option. Selected items are displayed as removable chips.



```tsx
export const MultiSelectExample = () => {
  const [values, setValues] = useState(['nextjs', 'vite']);
  return (
    <Combobox
      label="Platform Tools"
      multiple
      options={frameworks}
      value={values}
      onChange={setValues}
    />
  );
};
```

## Description & Feedback

You can add a `description` below the input to provide context or instructions.



```tsx
<Combobox 
  label="Deployment Target"
  description="Choose the region where your application will be deployed."
  options={regions}
/>
```

## States

The combobox supports different visual states like `disabled` or pre-filled values.



```tsx
<Combobox label="Disabled" disabled value="nextjs" options={frameworks} />
<Combobox label="Empty" options={[]} />
```

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `label` | `string` | - | An optional label displayed above the input. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Helper text displayed below the input. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `'Search or select...'` | Text displayed when no value is selected. |
| `options` | `ComboboxOption[]` | - | An array of { value, label } objects. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` | - | The current selected value(s). |
| `onChange` | `(value: string \| string[]) => void` | - | Callback fired when option(s) are selected. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the combobox is interactive. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Allows selecting multiple options using Chips. |
| `clearSearchOnSelect` | `boolean` | `false` | If true, the search query will be cleared when an item is selected. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |

# Slider

A premium, interactive slider component for selecting a value from a range, featuring smooth animations and real-time feedback.

## Import

```tsx
import { Slider } from '@/dashkit/Slider/Slider'
```

## Installation

Add the slider component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add slider
```

## Basic Usage

A simple slider with a label and default range (0-100).



```tsx
<Slider label="Brightness" defaultValue={70} />
```

## With Description & Value

Provide more context with a description and show the current value bubble.



```tsx
<Slider 
  label="Opacity" 
  description="Adjust the transparency."
  showValue
  defaultValue={45}
/>
```

## Controlled State

Manage the slider value using React's `useState` for full control.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'

export function VolumeSettings() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(50)

  return (
    <Slider 
      label="Volume Level" 
      value={value} 
      onChange={setValue} 
      showValue
    />
  )
}
```

## Custom Ranges & Steps

Define custom `min`, `max`, and `step` values for precise control.



```tsx
<Slider label="Price Range ($)" min={10} max={500} step={5} showValue />
<Slider label="Rating" min={0} max={5} step={0.5} showValue />
```

## States

Supports disabled and focus states with consistent design system aesthetics.



```tsx
<Slider label="Disabled Slider" disabled defaultValue={30} />
```

## Props

Extends all native `InputHTMLAttributes` (except `type` and `onChange`), plus these specialties:



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `label` | `string` | - | Title text rendered above the slider. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Description text rendered below the label. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to display the current numeric value. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number) => void` | - | Callback triggered when the value changes. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |

# DateField

A premium, HeroUI-inspired input component for entering and editing date values with individual segments for Day, Month, and Year.

## Import

```tsx
import { DateField } from 'dashkit'
```

## Installation

Add the DateField component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add datefield
```

## Basic Usage

A basic `DateField` with a label.



```tsx
<DateField label="Birth Date" />
```

## With Description

Provide additional context using the `description` prop.



```tsx
<DateField 
  label="Event Date" 
  description="Select the date for your upcoming celebration." 
/>
```

## States

`DateField` supports various states such as disabled and required.



```tsx
<DateField label="Required Field" isRequired />
<DateField label="Disabled Field" disabled value={new Date()} />
```

## Validation

Use the `error` prop to display validation feedback.



```tsx
<DateField 
  label="Expiry Date" 
  error="Please enter a valid future date." 
/>
```

## Controlled

Manage the date value explicitly using the `value` and `onChange` props.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'

export function ControlledDateField() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(new Date())

  return (
    <DateField 
      label="Controlled Date" 
      value={value} 
      onChange={setValue} 
    />
  )
}
```

## Properties


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `label` | `string` | - | The title text displayed above the date field. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Helpful information rendered below the input segments. |
| `error` | `string` | - | Validation error message that replaces the description. |
| `value` | `Date \| null` | - | The current date instance managed by the component. |
| `onChange` | `(date: Date \| null) => void` | - | Callback triggered whenever a valid date is typed or the field is cleared. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, prevents all user interaction with the segments. |
| `isRequired` | `boolean` | `false` | Displays an asterisk next to the label and marks the field as mandatory. |


## DatePicker

- Slug: `datepicker`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add datepicker`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`

# DatePicker

A minimal, animated date selection component built with native React and Framer Motion. Ideal for dashboards and forms that require single date selection with a premium look.

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from 'dashkit'
```

## Installation

Add the Date Picker to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add datepicker
```

## Basic Usage

The `DatePicker` component provides a clean calendar interface for date selection.



```tsx
import { DatePicker } from 'dashkit';
import { useState } from 'react';

function Example() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>();

  return (
    <div className="max-w-xs">
      <DatePicker 
        label="Select Birthday" 
        value={date} 
        onChange={setDate} 
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled State

Pass a `value` and `onChange` handler to fully control the selection.



## Customization

You can provide custom labels, descriptions, and placeholders.



## API Reference

### DatePicker


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `Date` | - | The currently selected Date object. |
| `onChange` | `(date: Date) => void` | - | Callback triggered when a new date is selected. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Label text displayed above the input. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Helper text displayed below the input. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `'Select date'` | Placeholder when no date is selected. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the picker is interactable. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS for the outer container. |


## OtpInput

- Slug: `otpinput`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add otpinput`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

export const OtpInputDemo = () => {
  const [otp, setOtp] = useState('');
  const [isVerifying, setIsVerifying] = useState(false);
  const [isComplete, setIsComplete] = useState(false);

  const handleVerify = () => {
    setIsVerifying(true);
    setTimeout(() => {
      setIsVerifying(false);
      setIsComplete(true);
    }, 1500);
  };

  return (
    
      
        Two-Step Verification
        
          Enter the 6-digit code sent to your device.
        
      

      
        

        {isComplete ? (
          
            
            Verification successful
          
        ) : (
          
            Verify Code
          
        )}

        {!isComplete && (
          
            Didn't receive the code? Resend
          
        )}
      
    
  );
}

# OTP Input

A premium input component optimized for One-Time Passwords, featuring automatic focus shifting, digit masking, and full paste support.

## Import

```tsx
import { OtpInput } from '@/dashkit/OtpInput/OtpInput';
```

## Installation

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add otp-input
```

## Examples

### Security Verification

Integrating the OTP input into a verification workflow with controlled state and loading feedback.



```tsx
export function VerificationForm() {
  const [otp, setOtp] = useState('');
  
  return (
    <OtpInput 
      length={6} 
      value={otp} 
      onChange={setOtp} 
    />
  );
}
```

## Features

- **Auto-Focus Logic**: Automatically moves focus to the next field as the user types.
- **Smart Backspace**: Deletes the current character and moves focus back when backspace is pressed.
- **Paste Support**: Intelligently handles pasted content by distributing digits across all input fields.
- **Input Filtering**: Only accepts numeric input to prevent accidental character entries.
- **Accessibility**: Includes proper `inputMode` and `autoComplete` attributes for mobile device optimization.

## Properties


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `length` | `number` | `6` | Total number of digits for the OTP code. |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | The current value of the combined input string. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Callback triggered whenever any field value changes. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Prevent any interaction with the input fields. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS for individual digit containers. |
| `containerClassName` | `string` | - | Styles for the parent flex container. |

# Modal

A centered, layered dialog component that focuses user attention on critical information or actions.

## Import

```tsx
import { Modal, ModalHeader, ModalContent, ModalFooter } from '@/dashkit/Modal/Modal'
```

## Installation

Add the modal to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add modal
```

## Usage

The modal follows a strict **Composition-based API** for maximum flexibility and layout control.

### Basic Implementation



```tsx
<Modal isOpen={isOpen} onClose={close}>
  <ModalHeader onClose={close}>
    <h2>Project Overview</h2>
    <p>Review your latest project stats.</p>
  </ModalHeader>
  <ModalContent>
    <p>Main content area...</p>
  </ModalContent>
  <ModalFooter>
    <Button variant="outlined" onClick={close}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button onClick={save}>Save Changes</Button>
  </ModalFooter>
</Modal>
```

### Advanced Layouts

Use the footer for standardized action alignment.



```tsx
<Modal isOpen={isOpen} onClose={close} size="lg">
  <ModalHeader onClose={close}>
    <h2>Team Management</h2>
    <p>Invite and manage roles.</p>
  </ModalHeader>
  <ModalContent>
    <div className="team-list">
      {/* Team settings content */}
    </div>
  </ModalContent>
  <ModalFooter>
    <Button variant="outlined" onClick={close}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button onClick={save}>Save Changes</Button>
  </ModalFooter>
</Modal>
```

## Formats & Examples

### Alert Modal

Smaller modals with centered content for destructive actions.



```tsx
<Modal isOpen={isOpen} size="sm" className="text-center">
  <ModalContent>
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-6">
      <FiTrash2 size={40} className="text-red-500" />
      <h3>Delete workspace?</h3>
      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 w-full gap-2">
        <Button variant="outlined">Cancel</Button>
        <Button variant="filled">Confirm Delete</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </ModalContent>
</Modal>
```

### Full-Screen (Immersive)

The `full` size provides a take-over experience while maintaining focus on a single task.



```tsx
<Modal isOpen={isOpen} size="full">
  <ModalHeader onClose={close}>
    <h2>Immersive Editor</h2>
  </ModalHeader>
  <ModalContent className="h-full">
     <div className="h-full border-2 border-dashed rounded-[2.5rem]">
       {/* Editor area content */}
     </div>
  </ModalContent>
  <ModalFooter>
    <Button variant="outlined" onClick={close}>Exit</Button>
    <Button onClick={launch}>Launch</Button>
  </ModalFooter>
</Modal>
```

## Features

- **Spring-Based Animations**: Uses `framer-motion` for a premium scale/fade entry.
- **Backdrop Blur**: Softly blurs background content for better focus.
- **Body Scroll Lock**: Automatically prevents scrolling when the modal is active.
- **Portalled Rendering**: Renders at the document root to avoid layering issues.
- **Keyboard Accessible**: Closes instantly when the `Escape` key is pressed.

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` | - | Controls if the modal is shown. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | - | Callback fired when closing (ESC or click outside). |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| '2xl' \| 'full'` | `'md'` | The max-width of the internal container. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Composition sub-components (ModalHeader, ModalContent, ModalFooter). |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the modal container. |
