# Drawer

A premium panel component that slides in from the edges of the screen, providing a temporary surface for navigation, settings, or details. It uses a compositional pattern to give you full control over the header, content, and footer sections.

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerFooter
} from '@/dashkit/Drawer/Drawer'
```

## Installation

Add the drawer component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add drawer
```

## Basic Usage

The Drawer is controlled via the `isOpen` prop and requires an `onClose` callback. You can compose your drawer using the provided sub-components.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerFooter,
  Button
} from '@/dashkit'

export default function MyPage() {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setIsOpen(true)}>Open Drawer</Button>

      <Drawer
        isOpen={isOpen}
        onClose={() => setIsOpen(false)}
        position="right"
      >
        <DrawerHeader>Header</DrawerHeader>
        <DrawerContent className="min-h-[200px]">Content</DrawerContent>
        <DrawerFooter>Footer</DrawerFooter>
      </Drawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Positions

The component supports all four screen edges, with smooth spring animations tailored for each.

- `right` (Default): Slides from the right.
- `left`: Slides from the left.
- `top`: Slides from the top.
- `bottom`: Slides from the bottom.

## Features

- **Spring Physics**: Natural, bouncy transitions using Framer Motion.
- **Backdrop Blur**: Softly blurs content behind the drawer for focus.
- **Gesture Support**: Swipe the drawer towards its edge to close it instantly.
- **Body Lock**: Automatically prevents background scrolling when open.
- **Compositional**: Use `DrawerHeader`, `DrawerContent`, and `DrawerFooter` for modular layouts.
- **Responsive**: Adapts its width or height based on the `size` prop or position.

## Props

### Drawer


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` | - | Controls the visibility of the drawer. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | - | Callback fired when the drawer should close. |
| `position` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom'` | `'right'` | The edge from which the drawer slides. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Custom width/height (Tailwind class e.g. max-w-xl). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Compositional components (Header, Content, Footer). |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom classes for the drawer container. |


### Sub-components

The sub-components `DrawerHeader`, `DrawerContent`, and `DrawerFooter` all accept `children` and an optional `className`.

- `DrawerHeader`: Standard padding and vertical layout for titles/descriptions.
- `DrawerContent`: Auto-scrolling container with custom scrollbars.
- `DrawerFooter`: Bottom-aligned flex container for action buttons.

# Dropdown Menu

An interactive menu that displays a list of actions or options when triggered.

## Import

```tsx
import { 
  Dropdown, 
  DropdownTrigger, 
  DropdownContent, 
  DropdownItem, 
  DropdownLabel, 
  DropdownSeparator 
} from '@/dashkit/Dropdown/Dropdown';
```

## Installation

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add dropdown
```

## Basic Usage

A simple dropdown with items, labels, and separators.



```tsx
<Dropdown>
  <DropdownTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="filled">
      Options <FiChevronDown />
    </Button>
  </DropdownTrigger>
  <DropdownContent>
    <DropdownItem leftIcon={<FiUser />}>Profile</DropdownItem>
    <DropdownItem leftIcon={<FiSettings />}>Settings</DropdownItem>
    <DropdownSeparator />
    <DropdownItem destructive>Logout</DropdownItem>
  </DropdownContent>
</Dropdown>
```

## Selectable Items

Dropdown items can show a selected state, typically used for choosing an option from a list.



```tsx
export function SelectableExample() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState('Personal');

  return (
    <Dropdown>
      <DropdownTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="outlined">{selected}</Button>
      </DropdownTrigger>
      <DropdownContent>
        <DropdownItem 
          selected={selected === 'Personal'} 
          onClick={() => setSelected('Personal')}
        >
          Personal
        </DropdownItem>
        <DropdownItem 
          selected={selected === 'Work'} 
          onClick={() => setSelected('Work')}
        >
          Work
        </DropdownItem>
      </DropdownContent>
    </Dropdown>
  );
}
```

## Custom Triggers

The `asChild` prop allows any element to act as the dropdown trigger, from icon buttons to text links.



```tsx
{/* Icon Button */}
<Dropdown align="right">
  <DropdownTrigger asChild>
    <button className="...">
      <FiSettings size={20} />
    </button>
  </DropdownTrigger>
  <DropdownContent>
    <DropdownLabel>Settings</DropdownLabel>
    <DropdownItem>Account</DropdownItem>
    <DropdownItem>Security</DropdownItem>
  </DropdownContent>
</Dropdown>

{/* Text Link */}
<Dropdown>
  <DropdownTrigger asChild>
    <button className="text-sky-500 font-semibold underline">
      Actions <FiChevronDown />
    </button>
  </DropdownTrigger>
  <DropdownContent>
    <DropdownItem>Download PDF</DropdownItem>
    <DropdownItem>Export CSV</DropdownItem>
  </DropdownContent>
</Dropdown>
```

## Features

- **Animated**: Uses Framer Motion for smooth scale and opacity transitions.
- **Accessible**: Closes automatically when clicking outside or selecting an item. Supports `Escape` key.
- **Customizable**: Supports custom triggers via `asChild`, alignment (`left` or `right`), and icons.
- **Styled**: Beautiful default styles for light and dark modes.

## Component API

### DropdownContent


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `align` | `'left' \| 'right'` | `'left'` | The alignment of the dropdown menu relative to the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the content container. |



### DropdownItem


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `leftIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon positioned to the left of the item text. |
| `rightIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon positioned to the right of the item text. |
| `destructive` | `boolean` | `false` | If true, applies red "destructive" styling. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | If true, applies a selected state with a checkmark. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction with the item. |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | - | Callback when the item is clicked. |


## Popover

- Slug: `popover`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add popover`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`

# Popover

A floating container that displays rich content anchored to a trigger element. Popovers are ideal for more complex content than tooltips, such as forms or descriptive text.

## Import

```tsx
import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent } from 'dashkit'
```

## Installation

Add the popover to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add popover
```

## Basic Usage

The `Popover` component uses a composition-based API. Wrap your trigger and content in the `Popover` provider.

```tsx
import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent, Button } from 'dashkit';

export default () => (
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTrigger asChild>
      <Button variant="outlined">Open Popover</Button>
    </PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent align="center" side="bottom">
      <div className="p-4">
        <h4 className="font-bold">Settings</h4>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Manage your account preferences.</p>
      </div>
    </PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
);
```

## Placement

Popovers can be placed on any side of the trigger using the `side` prop, and aligned using the `align` prop.

```tsx
<PopoverContent side="top" align="center">...</PopoverContent>
<PopoverContent side="right" align="center">...</PopoverContent>
<PopoverContent side="bottom" align="center">...</PopoverContent>
<PopoverContent side="left" align="center">...</PopoverContent>
```

## Trigger Mode

You can change how the popover is triggered using the `trigger` prop. It supports `click` (default) and `hover`.

```tsx
<Popover trigger="click">...</Popover>
<Popover trigger="hover">...</Popover>
```

## Custom Content

Since the `PopoverContent` is just a container, you can put any React components inside it.

## Features

- **Automatic Collision Handling**: The popover will flip to the opposite side if it doesn't have enough space in the preferred direction.
- **Escape to Close**: Pressing the `Escape` key closes the popover immediately.
- **Click Outside**: Automatically closes when user clicks outside the content or trigger.
- **Dynamic Portaling**: Renders via `createPortal` to avoid z-index and overflow issues.
- **Framer Motion Animations**: Smooth scale and opacity transitions.

## API

### PopoverContent Props

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The content to be displayed within the popover. |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `'bottom'` | Preferred side for the popover content. |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'center'` | Alignment along the specified side. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `8` | The distance in pixels from the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the content container. |


## Tooltip

- Slug: `tooltip`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add tooltip`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# Tooltip

A small popup that displays information when a user hovers over an element.

## Import

```tsx
import { 
  Tooltip, 
  TooltipTrigger, 
  TooltipContent 
} from '@/dashkit/Tooltip/Tooltip';
```

## Installation

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add tooltip
```

## Basic Usage

Tooltips are triggered by hovering over the trigger element.



```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outlined">
      <FiInfo /> Hover me
    </Button>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>
    Display helpful information
  </TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

## Side Positioning

Tooltips can be positioned on the `top`, `bottom`, `left`, or `right` of the trigger.



```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outlined">Left Tooltip</Button>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent side="left">
    I am on the left!
  </TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

## Features

- **Animated**: Uses Framer Motion for smooth entry and exit transitions.
- **Accessible**: Closes automatically when the mouse leaves the trigger.
- **Smart Positioning**: Automatically calculates the best position relative to the trigger.
- **Portalled**: Renders at the end of the document body to avoid z-index and overflow issues.
- **Design System Consistent**: Uses theme-aware popover tokens and radius variables.

## Component API

### Tooltip


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | The delay in milliseconds before the tooltip appears. |


### TooltipContent


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `'top'` | The side of the trigger to display the tooltip. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `8` | The distance in pixels between the trigger and the tooltip. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the content container. |


## Toast

- Slug: `toast`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add toast`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`

export const ToastExamples = () => {
  const showStacked = () => {

  };

  return (
    
      }>
        Trigger Stacked Toasts
      
       toast({ title: 'Deleted', description: 'The project has been removed.', type: 'error' })}

# Toast

A succinct message that provides feedback about an operation in a small, non-intrusive card.

## Installation

Add the toast component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add toast
```

## Setup

Wrap your application (usually in `main.tsx` or `App.tsx`) with the `ToastProvider`.

```tsx
import { ToastProvider } from '@/dashkit/Toast/Toast'

function App() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider position="bottom-right">
      <YourApp />
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

## Import

```tsx
import { toast, ToastProvider, useToast } from '@/dashkit/Toast/Toast'
```

## Basic Usage

Trigger a toast from anywhere by calling the `toast` function. Toasts automatically stack as cards to save space.



```tsx
import { toast } from '@/dashkit'

const notify = () => {
  toast({
    title: "Project Saved",
    description: "Your changes are now live.",
    type: "success",
  })
}
```

## Positioning

Supports multiple screen positions for different layout requirements.



```tsx
toast({ title: "Alert", position: "top-center" })
toast({ title: "Feedback", position: "top-right" })
```

## Inverted Theme

Enable the `invert` property on a specific toast (or globally at the `ToastProvider`) to render it with high-contrast, inverted colors. This is especially useful for making critical messages pop out.



```tsx
toast({ 
  title: "Archived", 
  description: "The conversation was moved to archives.", 
  invert: true 
})
```

## Features

- **Stacked Visualization**: Toasts stack vertically, revealing themselves as the top ones are dismissed.
- **Portalled Layout**: Renders at the document root to avoid z-index layering issues.
- **Framer Motion**: Smooth, spring-based entry/exit and layout animations.
- **Auto-dismiss**: Configurable duration with a default of 5 seconds.

## API Reference

### ToastProvider


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `position` | `ToastPosition` | `'bottom-right'` | Global default position for all toasts. |
| `invert` | `boolean` | `false` | If true, all toasts will render with inverted high-contrast colors by default. |


### toast(options)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `title` | `string` | - | Bold heading for the toast. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Body text for the message. |
| `type` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'error'` | `'default'` | Semantic style preset. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Explicit icon override. |
| `duration` | `number` | `5000` | MS before hiding (0 for persistent). |
| `position` | `ToastPosition` | `provider default` | Specific override for this toast. |
| `invert` | `boolean` | `provider default` | Override the global provider's invert setting for this specific toast. |


## Backdrop

- Slug: `backdrop`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add backdrop`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# Backdrop

A blurred or semi-transparent full-screen overlay, often used behind modals, drawers, or to dim the background for focus.

## Import

```tsx
import { Backdrop } from '@/dashkit/Backdrop/Backdrop'
```

## Installation

Add the backdrop to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add backdrop
```

## Basic Usage

The backdrop component is usually controlled by a state.

export const BasicExample = () => {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
       setShow(true)}>Show Backdrop
       setShow(false)} />
    </>
  );
};



```tsx
const [show, setShow] = useState(false);

return (
  <>
    <Button onClick={() => setShow(true)}>Show Backdrop</Button>
    <Backdrop show={show} onClick={() => setShow(false)} />
  </>
);
```

## With Children

You can pass children to the backdrop, which will be centered on top of the overlay.

export const ChildrenExample = () => {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
       setShow(true)}>Show Overlay with Content
       setShow(false)}>
        
          Centered Content
          This content is perfectly centered on top of the backdrop.
           setShow(false)}>Close
        
      
    </>
  );
};



```tsx
<Backdrop show={show} onClick={() => setShow(false)}>
  <div className="bg-card p-6 rounded-lg shadow-xl max-w-sm text-center">
    <h3 className="text-lg font-bold mb-2">Centered Content</h3>
    <Button onClick={() => setShow(false)}>Close</Button>
  </div>
</Backdrop>
```

## Props


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `show` | `boolean` | `true` | Controls the visibility of the backdrop. |
| `blur` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to apply a backdrop-blur-sm effect. |
| `transparent` | `boolean` | `false` | If true, the background color and blur will be hidden. |
| `fixed` | `boolean` | `true` | If true, use fixed positioning. If false, use absolute positioning relative to the parent. |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | - | Callback function when the backdrop is clicked. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Centered content to render on top of the backdrop. |


## Spinner

- Slug: `spinner`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add spinner`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# Spinner

A sleek, high-performance loading indicator built with SVG and CSS animations.

## Import

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@/dashkit/Spinner/Spinner'
```

## Installation

Add the spinner to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add spinner
```

## Basic Usage

The basic spinner uses a standard size and the current text color.



```tsx
<Spinner />
```

## Sizes

Use the `size` prop to scale the spinner. The default is 24px.



```tsx
<Spinner size={16} />
<Spinner size={24} />
<Spinner size={32} />
<Spinner size={48} />
```

## Colors

The spinner accepts any valid CSS color. It defaults to `currentColor` for easier theme integration.



```tsx
<Spinner color="#10b981" />
<Spinner color="#3b82f6" />
<Spinner color="#f59e0b" />
<Spinner color="#ef4444" />
```

## Thickness

Adjust the `thickness` of the spinner's stroke for different visual densities.



```tsx
<Spinner thickness={1} />
<Spinner thickness={2} />
<Spinner thickness={3} />
<Spinner thickness={4} />
```

## Context Integration

Spinners are commonly used alongside text labels to indicate specific processing states.



```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <Spinner size={18} color="#3b82f6" />
  <span>Loading...</span>
</div>
```

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `size` | `number` | `24` | Size of the spinner in pixels. |
| `color` | `string` | `'currentColor'` | Hex, RGB, or valid CSS color for the spinner. |
| `thickness` | `number` | `2` | Stroke width of the spinner. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |


## ProgressBar

- Slug: `progressbar`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add progressbar`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

# ProgressBar

Animated, fluid indicators for tracking task completion, loading states, or data metrics with high precision.

## Import

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from '@/dashkit/ProgressBar/ProgressBar'
```

## Installation

Add the progress bar into your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add progressbar
```

## Basic Usage

A simple progress bar with a controlled value. It uses spring-based animations for width changes by default.



```tsx
<ProgressBar value={65} showLabel />
```

## Colors

The component supports all semantic color palettes from your design system.



```tsx
<ProgressBar value={100} color="success" showLabel label="Deployment Complete" />
<ProgressBar value={75} color="primary" showLabel label="Uploading Assets" />
<ProgressBar value={85} color="base" showLabel label="NVMe Block Storage" />
```

## Sizes

Choose from four predefined heights to fit different UI contexts.



```tsx
<ProgressBar size="xs" value={60} />
<ProgressBar size="sm" value={70} />
<ProgressBar size="md" value={80} />
<ProgressBar size="lg" value={90} />
```

## Label Positions

Labels can be placed either above the bar or to the side, which is ideal for compact layouts like table cells.



```tsx
// Stacked layout (default)
<ProgressBar value={45} showLabel labelPosition="top" />

// Inline layout
<ProgressBar value={88} showLabel labelPosition="side" />
```

## API Reference

### ProgressBar Props


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `number` | `0` | Current value of the progress bar. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | The target/maximum value. |
| `color` | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info' \| 'base'` | `'primary'` | Color theme for the progress indicator fill. |
| `size` | `ProgressBarSize` | `'sm'` | Height variant (xs, sm, md, lg). |
| `showLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Display the percentage text. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Custom descriptive text. |
| `labelPosition` | `'top' \| 'side'` | `'top'` | Layout strategy for the labels. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | Spring-based width transitions. |


## CircularProgress

- Slug: `circularprogress`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add circularprogress`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# CircularProgress

A high-fidelity circular progress indicator built with SVG and Framer Motion. It provides smooth, fluid animations for status monitoring, health metrics, and loading states.

## Import

```tsx
import { CircularProgress } from '@/dashkit/CircularProgress/CircularProgress'
```

## Installation

Add the component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add circular-progress
```

## Basic Usage

The component accepts a `value` between 0 and 100. Use `showValue` to display the percentage inside the circle.



```tsx
<CircularProgress value={75} showValue />
<CircularProgress value={45} color="success" showValue />
<CircularProgress value={92} color="info" showValue />
<CircularProgress value={18} color="danger" showValue />
```

## Variants

Dashkit provides two visual variants: `solid` (default) for a crisp high-contrast track, and `soft` for a more integrated, subtle look.



```tsx
<CircularProgress value={65} variant="solid" showValue />
<CircularProgress value={65} variant="soft" color="success" showValue />
```

## Sizes

Choose from predefined sizes (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) or provide a custom numeric value for the diameter (in pixels).



```tsx
<CircularProgress value={30} size="sm" showValue />
<CircularProgress value={60} size="md" showValue />
<CircularProgress value={90} size="lg" showValue />
<CircularProgress value={50} size={120} showValue />
```

## Track Customization

You can explicitly set the color of the background track using the `trackColor` prop. This is useful when you want to deviate from the theme's default track styles.



```tsx
<CircularProgress value={70} trackColor="text-ds-200 dark:text-ds-700" />
<CircularProgress value={45} trackColor="text-emerald-500/10" color="success" />
```


## Custom Thickness

The `strokeWidth` prop allows you to override the default thickness of the track and indicator.



```tsx
<CircularProgress value={60} strokeWidth={2} showValue />
<CircularProgress value={60} strokeWidth={12} showValue />
```

## Minimalist Styles

Control the visibility of the background track and the shape of the progress ends using `showTrack` and `roundCaps`.



```tsx
<CircularProgress value={65} showTrack={false} showValue />
<CircularProgress value={65} roundCaps={false} showValue />
```

## API


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `number` | `0` | The current progress value (0-100). |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| number` | `'md'` | The diameter of the circular progress indicator in pixels or predefined sizes. |
| `color` | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'primary'` | The color theme of the indicator. |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'soft'` | `'solid'` | The visual variant of the background track. |
| `showTrack` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to show the background circle (track). |
| `roundCaps` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to use rounded ends for the progress indicator. |
| `strokeWidth` | `number` | `Predefined` | Custom thickness for the progress lines. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to display the progress percentage inside the circle. |
| `trackColor` | `string` | `-` | Explicit color class for the background track (overrides variant defaults). |
| `className` | `string` | `-` | Additional CSS classes for custom styling. |


## Skeleton

- Slug: `skeleton`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add skeleton`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

export const SkeletonDemo = () => {
  return (
    
      
        
        
          
          
        
      

      
        
        
          
          
          
        
      
    
  );
};

# Skeleton

A placeholder component used to mimic the layout of actual content while it is loading.

## Import

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@/dashkit/Skeleton/Skeleton'
```

## Installation

Add the skeleton to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add skeleton
```

## Demo



## Text Variant

Use the `variant="text"` prop for text line placeholders.



```tsx
<div className="space-y-2">
  <Skeleton variant="text" className="w-[40%]" />
  <Skeleton variant="text" className="w-[60%]" />
</div>
```

## Circular Variant

Use the `variant="circular"` prop for avatars or circular elements.



```tsx
<Skeleton variant="circular" className="size-12" />
```

## Rectangular Variant

The default `variant="rectangular"` is ideal for cards, images, or large content blocks.



```tsx
<Skeleton variant="rectangular" className="h-[200px] w-full" />
```

## Animation

By default, skeletons use a `shimmer` animation. 



```tsx
<div className="space-y-4">
  <Skeleton variant="rectangular" className="h-24 w-full" />
  <div className="space-y-2">
    <Skeleton variant="text" />
    <Skeleton variant="text" className="w-[80%]" />
  </div>
</div>
```

## Pulse Animation

Use the `animation="pulse"` prop for a classic fading effect. This provides a more subtle "breathing" feel to your placeholders.



```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
  <Skeleton variant="circular" className="size-12" animation="pulse" />
  <div className="flex-1 space-y-2">
    <Skeleton variant="text" className="w-[40%]" animation="pulse" />
    <Skeleton variant="text" className="w-[60%]" animation="pulse" />
  </div>
</div>
```

## No Animation

Disable animations entirely with `animation="none"`.



```tsx
<Skeleton animation="none" />
```

## API



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `variant` | `'text' \| 'circular' \| 'rectangular'` | `'rectangular'` | The shape of the skeleton. |
| `animation` | `'shimmer' \| 'pulse' \| 'none'` | `'shimmer'` | The animation effect to use. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for custom sizing and styling. |


## FloatActionMenu

- Slug: `float-action-menu`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add float-action-menu`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`
- Dashkit Dependencies: `iconbutton`

export const FloatActionMenuDemo = () => (
  
    
      
        Slide-in Interaction
      
      
        The button remains fixed while the menu slides in from the right to left.
      
    

    }
      position="bottom-right"
      className="absolute"
    >
      
        {[
          { icon: , label: 'Enable Alerts', color: 'text-orange-500' },
          { icon: , label: 'View messages', color: 'text-emerald-500' },
          { icon: , label: 'Global Settings', color: 'text-ds-500' },
          { icon: , label: 'My profile', color: 'text-blue-500' },
        ].map((item, i) => (
          
            {item.label}
          
        ))}
      
    
  
)

# Float Action Menu

A premium floating action button that reveals an interactive menu card sliding from right to left.

## Usage

```tsx
import { FloatActionMenu } from 'dashkit'
import { FiCommand, FiPlus, FiUsers } from 'react-icons/fi'

export function MyComponent() {
  return (
    <FloatActionMenu label="Actions" icon={<FiCommand />}>
      <div className="space-y-4">
        <button className="flex items-center gap-2 w-full p-2 hover:bg-ds-50 rounded-lg">
          <FiPlus className="size-4" />
          <span>New Project</span>
        </button>
        <button className="flex items-center gap-2 w-full p-2 hover:bg-ds-50 rounded-lg">
          <FiUsers className="size-4" />
          <span>Invite Team</span>
        </button>
      </div>
    </FloatActionMenu>
  )
}
```

## Interactive Demo

The demo below showcases the snappy, right-to-left slide transition. The button remains visible and acts as a toggle while the menu is open.


  


## Positions

The menu can be positioned at any corner of the parent container or screen.

```tsx
<FloatActionMenu position="bottom-right" label="Bottom Right" />
<FloatActionMenu position="bottom-left" label="Bottom Left" />
<FloatActionMenu position="top-right" label="Top Right" />
<FloatActionMenu position="top-left" label="Top Left" />
```

### Category: Data Display & Metrics

## Avatar

- Slug: `avatar`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add avatar`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

# Avatar

A versatile component for presenting user profile pictures, with built-in fallback Support and smooth loading transitions.

## Installation

Add the Avatar to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add avatar
```

## Basic usage

By default, the Avatar component will show initials as a fallback if the image source is not provided or fails to load.



```tsx
import { Avatar } from 'dashkit'

function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Avatar src="..." alt="John Doe" />
      <Avatar alt="Jane Smith" />
      <Avatar fallback="JD" className="bg-blue-500 text-white" />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Sizes

Available in five standard sizes: `xs`, `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`, and `xl`.



## Shapes

Choose between `circle` (default) and `square` shapes.



## Avatar Group

Cluster multiple avatars together with automatic truncation using the `max` prop.



```tsx
<AvatarGroup max={3}>
  <Avatar src="..." />
  <Avatar src="..." />
  <Avatar src="..." />
  <Avatar src="..." />
</AvatarGroup>
```

## API Reference

### Avatar


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `src` | `string` | - | The image source URL. |
| `alt` | `string` | - | Alt text (also used for initials fallback). |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` | - | Custom fallback content. |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Horizontal/vertical dimensions. |
| `shape` | `'circle' \| 'square'` | `'circle'` | The border radius style. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to show a focus-like ring border. |


### AvatarGroup


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `max` | `number` | - | Maximum visible avatars. |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Size for all child avatars. |
| `spacing` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Overlap distance between avatars. |


## Badge

- Slug: `badge`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add badge`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`

# Badge

Visual indicators used for counts, statuses, or high-priority labels. Dashkit provides two distinct badge components optimized for different use cases.

## Import

```tsx
import { Badge, FloatBadge } from '@/dashkit/Badge'
```

## Installation

Add the badge to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add badge
```

## Standalone Badge

Use the `Badge` component for simple labels or indicators.



```tsx
import { Badge } from 'dashkit';

export default () => (
  <div className="flex gap-4">
    <Badge content="Live" color="success" pulse />
    <Badge content="Experimental" color="info" />
    <Badge content="Critical" color="danger" />
    <Badge dot pulse color="success" />
  </div>
);
```

## Floating Badge 

Use the `FloatBadge` component to wrap an element and position a badge relative to its corners.



```tsx
import { FloatBadge, Button } from 'dashkit';
import { FiMail } from 'react-icons/fi';

export default () => (
  <FloatBadge content={5} color="danger" position="top-right">
    <Button variant="outlined" leftIcon={<FiMail />}>
      Messages
    </Button>
  </FloatBadge>
);
```

## Badge Positions

Dot badges can be positioned at any corner of the element.



```tsx
<FloatBadge dot position="top-right">...</FloatBadge>
<FloatBadge dot position="top-left">...</FloatBadge>
<FloatBadge dot position="bottom-right">...</FloatBadge>
<FloatBadge dot position="bottom-left">...</FloatBadge>
```

## Status Indicators

Combine badges with other components to create rich status indicators.



```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <Badge dot color="success" pulse />
  <span className="text-sm font-semibold">Server Online</span>
</div>
```

## Features

- **Automatic Clipping**: Numbers larger than the `max` prop (default 99) are automatically formatted with a plus sign (e.g., `99+`).
- **Pulse Effects**: Easily add a status pulse animation to dots or small content badges via the `pulse` prop.
- **Rhythmic Corners**: All text-based badges now use a modern `rounded-sm` style, while dots remain `rounded-full`.
- **Flexible Variants**: Choose between `solid` and `outline` appearances.

## API

### Badge Props



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `content` | `ReactNode` | - | Content to display inside the badge. |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'soft' \| 'outline'` | `'solid'` | Styling variant (solid, soft pastel, or bordered outline). |
| `color` | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info' \| 'base'` | `'success'` | Color palette (success, warning, danger, info). |
| `pulse` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a pulse animation layer. |
| `dot` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders as a small dot without content. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the badge is visible (with entry/exit animation). |
| `max` | `number` | `99` | Max number to display (e.g., 99+). |



### FloatBadge Props

`FloatBadge` inherits all `Badge` props and adds the following:



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The element the badge will be attached to. |
| `position` | `BadgePosition` | `'top-right'` | Placement (top-right, top-left, bottom-right, bottom-left). |
| `offset` | `[number, number]` | - | Custom [x, y] offset in pixels. |


## FloatBadge

- Slug: `floatbadge`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add floatbadge`
- Dashkit Dependencies: `badge`

export const MultiSelectExample = () => {
  const [selectedChips, setSelectedChips] = useState(['React', 'Vite']);
  const toggleChip = (label) => {
    setSelectedChips(prev =>
      prev.includes(label) ? prev.filter(c => c !== label) : [...prev, label]

      {['React', 'Next.js', 'Vite', 'Tailwind', 'Framer'].map(tech => (

# Chip

A compact, interactive element that represents an input, attribute, or action, inspired by Material Design 3.

## Import

```tsx
import { Chip } from '@/dashkit/Chip/Chip'
```

## Installation

Add the chip component to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add chip
```

## Basic Usage

The basic tonal chip represents a simple label or filter item.



```tsx
<Chip label="Personal" />
<Chip label="Work" />
<Chip label="Urgent" />
```

## Types

Chips can be used for different purposes, and their visual behavior changes based on provided props.



```tsx
import { FiClock, FiSettings } from 'react-icons/fi';

<Chip label="Assist Chip" icon={<FiClock />} onClick={() => {}} />
<Chip label="Filter Chip" selected onClick={() => {}} />
<Chip label="Input Chip" onDelete={() => {}} />
<Chip label="Action Chip" icon={<FiSettings />} color="info" />
```

## Visual Styles

Chips combine three `variants` with five semantic `colors` to provide maximum flexibility for different UI contexts.



```tsx
// Using different variants
<Chip label="Tonal" variant="tonal" />
<Chip label="Filled" variant="filled" />
<Chip label="Outlined" variant="outlined" />

// Combining with colors
<Chip label="Success" color="success" variant="filled" />
<Chip label="Danger" color="danger" variant="tonal" />
```

## Multi-Selection

Selection state shows a checkmark icon automatically. This is useful for filter situations.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';

export const MultiSelectExample = () => {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(['React']);
  const toggle = (label) => {
    setSelected(prev =>
      prev.includes(label) ? prev.filter(c => c !== label) : [...prev, label]
    );
  };

  return (
    <div className="flex gap-3">
      {['React', 'Vite', 'Next.js'].map(tech => (
        <Chip
          key={tech}
          label={tech}
          selected={selected.includes(tech)}
          variant="outlined"
          onClick={() => toggle(tech)}
        />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};
```

## Removable Labels

Chips can include a delete action, useful for tag systems.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';

export const RemovableExample = () => {
  const [chips, setChips] = useState(['Work', 'Personal']);
  const remove = (label) => setChips(prev => prev.filter(c => c !== label));

  return (
    <div className="flex gap-3">
      {chips.map(tag => (
        <Chip key={tag} label={tag} onDelete={() => remove(tag)} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};
```

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Content displayed inside the chip. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Optional icon displayed before the label. |
| `variant` | `ChipVariant` | `'tonal'` | Visual style of the chip: filled, outlined, tonal. |
| `color` | `ChipColor` | `'base'` | Color theme of the chip: base, success, warning, danger, info. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a checkmark icon to indicate selection. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Prevents user interaction and fades the component. |
| `onClick` | `function` | - | Called when the chip body is clicked. |
| `onDelete` | `function` | - | Called when the remove icon is clicked. Adds the icon if present. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container. |


## ListTile

- Slug: `listtile`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add listtile`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# List Tile

A flexible row component for building lists, menus, and settings panels. Supports leading icons or avatars, a title and subtitle text block, and a trailing slot for actions or indicators.

## Import

```tsx
import { ListTile } from '@/dashkit/ListTile'
```

## Installation

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add listtile
```

## Basic Usage



```tsx
<ListTile title="Account" leading={<FiUser size={18} />} trailing={<FiChevronRight size={16} />} interactive />
```

## With Subtitle



```tsx
<ListTile
  title="Ana Lima"
  subtitle="ana@example.com"
  leading={<Avatar fallback="AL" size="sm" />}
  trailing={<Badge content="Admin" color="info" />}
/>
```

## With Trailing Control



```tsx
<ListTile
  title="Email Notifications"
  subtitle="Receive updates via email"
  leading={<FiMail size={18} />}
  trailing={<Switch defaultChecked />}
/>
```

## Disabled State



```tsx
<ListTile title="Disabled Item" disabled interactive />
```

## Dividers

Use the `divider` prop to render a bottom border directly on each tile. This lets you manage separators per-tile without a wrapper, which is useful when bleed-edge layouts remove the container.



```tsx
<ListTile title="Profile" divider interactive />
<ListTile title="Notifications" divider interactive />
<ListTile title="Privacy" interactive />
```

You can also use `divider` on all but the last item via array index:

```tsx
{items.map((item, i, arr) => (
  <ListTile
    key={item.label}
    title={item.label}
    divider={i < arr.length - 1}
  />
))}
```

## Props (API)


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `title` | `React.ReactNode` | - | Primary text content of the tile. |
| `subtitle` | `React.ReactNode` | - | Secondary descriptive text rendered below the title. |
| `leading` | `React.ReactNode` | - | Content rendered on the left side (icon, avatar, etc.). |
| `trailing` | `React.ReactNode` | - | Content rendered on the right side (chevron, badge, switch, etc.). |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `auto` | Enables hover/active styles and keyboard interaction. Auto-detected when onClick is provided. |
| `divider` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders a bottom border on the tile, acting as a separator between items. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Dims the tile and disables all interactions. |
| `onClick` | `MouseEventHandler` | - | Click handler. Setting this automatically enables interactive mode. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the root element. |


## StatsCard

- Slug: `statscard`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add statscard`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`
- Dashkit Dependencies: `card`, `animatenumber`, `divider`

# Stats Card

A high-level component for displaying key performance indicators, metrics, and trends at a glance.

## Import

```tsx
import { StatsCard } from '@/dashkit/StatsCard/StatsCard'
```

## Installation

Add the stats card to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add statscard
```

## Basic Usage

The `StatsCard` is perfect for dashboards and summary sections.

  
  
  

```tsx
import { StatsCard } from 'dashkit';

export default () => (
  <div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-6">
    <StatsCard
      title="Total Revenue"
      value={48250}
      prefix="$"
      trend={12.5}
      trendLabel="vs last month"
      status="success"
    />
    <StatsCard
      title="Active Users"
      value={12403}
      trend={-2.4}
      status="danger"
    />
    <StatsCard
      title="Conversion Rate"
      value={3.42}
      suffix="%"
      precision={2}
    />
  </div>
);
```

## With Icons

Add visual context using icons from `react-icons`.

  }
    status="info"
    description="Completion across all active sprints"
  />
  }
    status="warning"
    trend={8}
    trendLabel="today"
    description="Unassigned support requests"
  />

```tsx
import { StatsCard } from 'dashkit';
import { HiOutlineChartBarSquare, HiOutlineTicket } from 'react-icons/hi2';

export default () => (
  <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-6">
    <StatsCard
      title="Project Progress"
      value={75}
      suffix="%"
      icon={<HiOutlineChartBarSquare />}
      status="info"
    />
    <StatsCard
      title="New Tickets"
      value={12}
      icon={<HiOutlineTicket />}
      status="warning"
    />
  </div>
);
```

## With Sparklines

Visualize data trends directly within the card using the `chart` prop.

  
  
  

```tsx
import { StatsCard } from 'dashkit';

export default () => (
  <StatsCard
    title="Sales Growth"
    value={8400}
    prefix="$"
    trend={24}
    status="success"
    chart={{
      data: [10, 25, 45, 30, 55, 70, 65, 90],
    }}
  />
);
```

## Chart and Description

Combine sparklines and descriptive footers for maximum context.

  
  

```tsx
import { StatsCard } from 'dashkit';

export default () => (
  <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-6">
    <StatsCard
      title="User Acquisition"
      value={1250}
      trend={15.4}
      status="success"
      description="New signups via organic search"
      chart={{
        data: [100, 120, 150, 140, 180, 210, 250],
      }}
    />
    <StatsCard
      title="System Latency"
      value={42}
      suffix="ms"
      trend={-5}
      status="danger"
      description="Response time for API v2"
      chart={{
        data: [50, 48, 45, 46, 42, 40, 42],
      }}
    />
  </div>
);
```

## API

### StatsCard Props

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `title` | `string` | - | The label for the metric. |
| `value` | `number` | - | The main numeric value to display. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `''` | Text to prepend to the value (e.g., $). |
| `suffix` | `string` | `''` | Text to append to the value (e.g., %). |
| `precision` | `number` | `0` | Number of decimal places for the value. |
| `trend` | `number` | - | Percentage change to display. |
| `trendLabel` | `string` | - | Explanatory text for the trend. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon element to display in the top-right. |
| `status` | `'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'neutral'` | `'neutral'` | Semantic status that controls trend colors and icons. |
| `description` | `string` | - | Supporting text displayed at the bottom. |
| `chart` | `{ data: number[], color?: string }` | - | Data for the sparkline chart. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable entry and number animations. |


## AnimateNumber

- Slug: `animatenumber`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add animatenumber`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

export const AnimateNumberExample = () => {
  const [val, setVal] = useState(1250);
  return (
    
      
        
      
      
          setVal(v => v + Math.floor(Math.random() * 100))}>Update Value
          setVal(1250)}>Reset
      
    
  );
}

# Animate Number

A specialized component for creating sleek numeric counters with independent digit animations. It uses a "top-to-bottom" sliding effect for each character, providing a premium and dynamic feel for dashboards and metrics.

## Import

```tsx
import { AnimateNumber } from '@/dashkit/AnimateNumber'
```

## Installation

Add the animate-number to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add animate-number
```

## Basic Usage

The component will automatically animate whenever the `value` prop changes. Each digit that differs from the previous value will slide vertically to its new position.



```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { AnimateNumber, Button } from 'dashkit';

export default () => {
  const [val, setVal] = useState(1250);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-6">
      <div className="text-5xl font-bold tracking-tighter tabular-nums">
        <AnimateNumber value={val} />
      </div>
      <div className="flex gap-4">
         <Button variant="soft" onClick={() => setVal(v => v + 50)}>Update</Button>
         <Button variant="outlined" onClick={() => setVal(1250)}>Reset</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};
```

## Advanced Examples

You can customize the precision, add prefixes/suffixes, and control the duration (speed of the slide animation).



## Features

- **Character Splitting**: Each digit animates independently for a premium odometer feel.
- **Top-to-Bottom Movement**: New values slide in from above while old ones exit below.
- **Localization Support**: Automatically handles thousands separators and decimal markers via `Intl.NumberFormat`.
- **Customizable Duration**: Control the speed of each character's vertical transition.

## API


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `number` | - | The target value to animate to. |
| `precision` | `number` | `0` | Number of decimal places to show. |
| `prefix` | `string` | - | String to display before the number. |
| `suffix` | `string` | - | String to display after the number. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.35` | Animation duration for each character in seconds. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'en-US'` | Locale for number formatting. |


## SystemLogs

- Slug: `systemlogs`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add systemlogs`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`
- Dashkit Dependencies: `badge`

# System Logs

A terminal-style component for displaying real-time system logs, process outputs, or audit trails with auto-scrolling and status indicators.

## Import

```tsx
import { SystemLogs, type LogEntry } from '@/dashkit/SystemLogs/SystemLogs'
```

## Installation

Add the system logs to your project using the Dashkit CLI:

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add systemlogs
```

## Usage

The `SystemLogs` component takes an array of `logs` and renders them in a dark, monospace container that mimics a terminal environment.

  

```tsx
import { SystemLogs } from '@/dashkit/SystemLogs/SystemLogs'

const logs = [
  { type: 'info', message: 'Starting deployment of version 2.4.0...', timestamp: '10:00:01' },
  { type: 'ok', message: 'Docker image pulled: alpine-node:20', timestamp: '10:00:05' },
  { type: 'info', message: 'Allocating resources in us-west-2...', timestamp: '10:00:08' },
  { type: 'stable', message: 'Health checks passed. Traffic routing enabled.', timestamp: '10:00:15' },
]

export default () => (
  <SystemLogs
    title="Cloud Deployment"
    session="worker-nodes-01"
    status="Running"
    statusColor="success"
    maxHeight={300}
    logs={logs}
  />
)
```

## Log Levels

The component supports five distinct log levels, each with its own visual style:

- `ok`: Success messages (indicated by `[OK]`)
- `info`: Informational messages (indicated by `[INF]`)
- `warn`: Warning messages (indicated by `[WRN]`)
- `error`: Error messages (indicated by `[ERR]`)
- `stable`: Stability or state updates (indicated by `[STB]`)

  

## Customization

### Auto-scrolling

By default, the component automatically scrolls to the bottom when new logs are added. You can disable this behavior by setting `autoScroll={false}`.

### Header & Footer

- `title`: The label displayed in the terminal header.
- `session`: An optional session identifier displayed in the footer.
- `status`: A status label displayed as a badge in the footer.
- `statusColor`: The color of the status badge.

## Props

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `logs` | `LogEntry[]` | - | An array of log entries to display. Each entry has a type, message, and optional timestamp. |
| `title` | `string` | `'System Logs'` | The title displayed in the terminal header. |
| `session` | `string` | - | Optional session ID or name displayed in the footer. |
| `status` | `string` | `'Stable'` | Status text displayed in the footer badge. |
| `statusColor` | `BadgeColor` | `'success'` | Color of the status badge in the footer. |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string` | - | Maximum height of the log container. Enables scrolling if logs exceed this height. |
| `autoScroll` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to automatically scroll to the bottom when new logs arrive. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the root container. |


## Table

- Slug: `table`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add table`
- NPM Dependencies: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `react-icons`

# Table

A simple, responsive table component for displaying structured data.

## Basic usage

Built with a composition pattern for ultimate flexibility. Renders a clean semantic table designed to be placed inside any container, card, or scrollable wrapper.




  Inventory list exported today.
  
    
      Invoice
      Status
      Method
      Amount
    
  
  
    
      INV001
      Paid
      Credit Card
      $250.00
    
    
      INV002
      Pending
      PayPal
      $150.00
    
    
      INV003
      Unpaid
      Bank Transfer
      $350.00
    
  
  
    
      Total: $750.00
    
  




## Actions Support

Tables often need a way to perform operations on specific rows. You can easily integrate a `Dropdown` for clean, consolidated actions.



  
    
      Customer
      Email
      Actions
    
  
  
    {[
      { name: 'John Cooper', email: 'john@example.com' },
      { name: 'Sarah Miller', email: 'sarah@example.com' },
    ].map((user) => (
      
        {user.name}
        {user.email}
        
          
            
              } variant="ghost" size="sm" />
            
            
              Actions
              View details
              Edit customer
              
              Delete customer
            
          
        
      
    ))}
  



```tsx
<Table>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Product</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Category</TableHead>
      <TableHead className="text-right">Price</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    <TableRow>
      <TableCell>Wireless Headphones</TableCell>
      <TableCell>Electronics</TableCell>
      <TableCell className="text-right">$199.99</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
    <TableRow>
      <TableCell>Smart Watch</TableCell>
      <TableCell>Accessories</TableCell>
      <TableCell className="text-right">$249.00</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

## API Reference

### TableContainer


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the horizontal scroll wrapper with custom scrollbar styling. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The table element. |



### Table


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the table element. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The table content (Header, Body, etc). |


### TableHead


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom styles for the header cell. |


### TableCell


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Custom styles for the body cell. |
| `colSpan` | `number` | - | The number of columns the cell should span. |


### Category: Visualization & Media

## AreaChart

- Slug: `areachart`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add areachart`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# Area Chart

The **AreaChart** component is a lightweight, responsive data visualization tool built using native SVG and **Framer Motion**. It's designed to be lean, performant, and deeply customizable through theme tokens.

## Examples

### Default Area Chart





### Weekly Performance (7 Values)

A standard weekly view using 7 consecutive data points.





```tsx
import { AreaChart } from 'dashkit';

function Example() {
  const data = [{ label: 'Jan', value: 10 }, { label: 'Feb', value: 25 }];
  const series = [{ key: 'value', label: 'Total Users', color: 'var(--color-blue-500)' }];

  return <AreaChart data={data} series={series} />;
}
```

### Multiple Series (Mobile vs Desktop)

Compare multiple data points using the `series` array.



```tsx
<AreaChart
  data={deviceData}
  series={[
    { key: 'mobile', label: 'Mobile Devices', color: 'var(--color-indigo-500)' },
    { key: 'desktop', label: 'Desktop Devices', color: 'var(--color-emerald-500)' }
  ]}
/>
```

### Market Trends (3+ Series)

Compare complex data sets with three or more series.





### Complex Analytics (7 Series)

Comparing seven different data streams simultaneously to demonstrate high-density visualization and overlapping areas.





### System Performance

Use a single series with specialized semantic colors for status monitoring.





## API Reference

### AreaChart



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `data` | `Record<string, string \| number>[]` | - | Array of objects containing data keys. |
| `series` | `AreaChartSeries[]` | - | Configuration for each data series to render. |
| `height` | `number \| string` | `'100%'` | Height of the chart container. |
| `showGrid` | `boolean` | `true` | Display dashed horizontal lines. |
| `showLabels` | `boolean` | `true` | Display X-axis labels. |
| `showTooltip` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable interactive tooltips. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable entrance animations. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS for the container. |


## BarChart

- Slug: `barchart`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add barchart`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# Bar Chart

The **BarChart** component is a powerful, animated data visualization tool built for comparing discrete categories or showing distribution across groups. It supports multiple grouped series, interactive tooltips, and smooth entrance animations.

## Examples

### Single Series Bar Chart





```tsx
import { BarChart } from 'dashkit';

function Example() {
  const data = [
    { label: 'Jan', value: 400 },
    { label: 'Feb', value: 300 },
    //...
  ];
  const series = [{ key: 'value', label: 'Revenue', color: 'var(--color-blue-500)' }];

  return <BarChart data={data} series={series} />;
}
```

### Grouped Bar Chart (Yearly Comparison)

Compare multiple metrics across the same time periods using grouped bars.





```tsx
<BarChart 
  data={userData} 
  series={[
    { key: 'active', label: 'Active', color: 'var(--color-emerald-500)' },
    { key: 'inactive', label: 'Inactive', color: 'var(--color-amber-500)' },
    { key: 'pending', label: 'Pending', color: 'var(--color-blue-500)' }
  ]}
/>
```

### Resource Allocation

Use semantic colors to visualize system performance or resource distribution.





### Textured Bars & Background Tracks

Apply SVG patterns to bars using the `texture` prop (`'striped' | 'dots' | 'grid' | 'gradient'`) and enable ghost background tracks with `showTrack`.





```tsx
<BarChart 
  data={planData} 
  series={[
    { key: 'count', label: 'Subscriptions', color: 'var(--color-primary)' }
  ]}
  texture="striped"
  showTrack
/>
```

## API Reference

### BarChart


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `data` | `Record<string, string \| number>[]` | - | Array of objects containing data keys. |
| `series` | `BarChartSeries[]` | - | Configuration for each data series to render. |
| `height` | `number \| string` | `'100%'` | Height of the chart container. |
| `barGap` | `number` | `4` | Spacing between individual bars within a group. |
| `rounded` | `boolean` | `true` | Apply rounded corners to bars. |
| `showGrid` | `boolean` | `true` | Display dashed horizontal lines. |
| `showLabels` | `boolean` | `true` | Display X-axis labels. |
| `showTooltip` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable interactive tooltips. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable entrance animations. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS for the container. |

## PieChart

- Slug: `piechart`
- Installation: `bunx carllosnc/dashkit add piechart`
- NPM Dependencies: `framer-motion`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`

# Pie Chart

The **PieChart** component is an expressive tool for visualizing categorical distributions. It features interactive segments with tooltips, smooth hover scaling, and supports donut variations via the `innerRadius` prop.

## Examples

### Classic Pie Chart





```tsx
import { PieChart } from 'dashkit';

function Example() {
  const data = [
    { label: 'Direct', value: 400, color: '#0ea5e9' },
    { label: 'Social', value: 300, color: '#f59e0b' },
    //...
  ];

  return <PieChart data={data} />;
}
```

### Donut Chart

Transform any pie chart into a donut chart by setting the `innerRadius` property (0 to 1).





```tsx
<PieChart 
  innerRadius={0.6} 
  data={userData} 
/>
```

## API Reference

### PieChart



| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `data` | `PieChartDataItem[]` | - | Array of objects with label, value, and color. |
| `innerRadius` | `number` | `0` | Radius of the center hole (0 for Pie, > 0 for Donut). |
| `showLabels` | `boolean` | `true` | Display the legend below the chart. |
| `showTooltip` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable interactive segment tooltips. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable entrance animations. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS for the container. |

# Image Expander

A premium component that enables cinematic image expansion with smooth animations, backdrop blur, and caption support.

## Import

```tsx
import { ImageExpander } from '@/dashkit/ImageExpander/ImageExpander';
```

## Installation

```bash
bunx carllosnc/dashkit add image-expander
```

## Examples

Building a clean gallery with expanding visuals.



```tsx
<ImageExpander 
  caption="Cinematic Waterfall"
  full={<img src="/large.jpg" className="w-auto h-auto max-h-[85vh] rounded-lg" />}
>
  <img src="/thumb.jpg" className="w-full h-full object-cover rounded-lg" />
</ImageExpander>
```

## Features

- **Spring Dynamics**: Natural, bouncy transitions powered by Framer Motion.
- **Glassmorphism**: Elegant backdrop blur and translucent overlays.
- **Compositional**: Supports any ReactNode as the thumbnail or full-size content.
- **Responsive**: Adapts perfectly to mobile and desktop viewports.
- **Esc to Close**: Closes automatically when the Escape key is pressed.

## Properties


| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The thumbnail content (usually an ). |
| `full` | `ReactNode` | `children` | The content to display in the expanded modal state. |
| `caption` | `string` | - | An optional label shown at the bottom of the expanded view. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Styles for the thumbnail container. |
